item.title: Exploring sex differences in global cancer incidence and mortality and the role of national development level.
item.dc:creator: Hoveling LA, Bergink-Voorthuis BJ, van Vlaardingen JRG, Verhoeven RHA, Wagner AD, Soerjomataram I, Siesling S
item.description:
Authors: Hoveling LA, Bergink-Voorthuis BJ, van Vlaardingen JRG, Verhoeven RHA, Wagner AD, Soerjomataram I, Siesling S
Journal: ESMO real world data and digital oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.esmorw.2026.100790
Published: 2026-Dec-01
PMID: 42959695



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We analysed sex differences in global cancer incidence and mortality using a national development index to better understand how broader socioeconomic factors may contribute to or mitigate sex differences in cancer outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Cancer incidence and mortality data (2012-2017) were obtained from the International Agency for Research on Cancer, covering 43 countries for incidence and 60 for mortality. Only nonsex-specific cancers were included and categorised into 12 groups. Age-standardised incidence rates (ASIR) and age-standardised mortality rates (ASMRs) were calculated, with sex differences analysed using men-to-women ratios (MWRs). Linear regression was used to assess the association between Human Development Index (HDI) and MWRs across cancer types. RESULTS: Among the cancer types included in this study, cancers of the colorectum, stomach, and lungs showed the highest incidence and mortality. Men are 12-13 times more likely to be diagnosed with oesophageal cancer (MWR ≈ 13), over nine times more likely to die from head and neck cancers, and >6 times more likely to die from lung cancer. Thyroid cancer incidence is up to five times higher in women than in men. No clear link was found between HDI and MWRs in incidence, but HDI relates to mortality and MWRs for several cancer types, with brain and thyroid cancers showing higher male mortality, while lung cancer showing relatively higher female mortality in high-HDI countries. CONCLUSIONS: Sex differences in cancer burden vary substantially across cancer types. National development was associated with sex differences in mortality, but not incidence, suggesting that factors related to health care and survival differ more between countries with different HDIs and contribute to these differences more than exposure to risk factors, which relates more to incidence.

item.title: Dynamic Voice Computed Tomography for Dysphonia Disproportionate to Clinical Findings.
item.dc:creator: Larson PJ, Schuman AD, Friedman AD, Dion GR, Burch MB, Howell RJ
item.description:
Authors: Larson PJ, Schuman AD, Friedman AD, Dion GR, Burch MB, Howell RJ
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71001
Published: 2026-Nov-02
PMID: 42972625



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Accurate evaluation of glottic anatomy in adults with dysphonia can be challenging when videostroboscopy is limited by altered anatomy, supraglottic hyperfunction, or posterior glottic pathology. We sought to evaluate the clinical utility of Dynamic Voice Computed Tomography (DVCT) in complex adult voice patients with prior laryngeal framework surgery or suspected posterior glottic insufficiency (PGI). METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of 15 adult patients undergoing DVCT for evaluation of dysphonia at a tertiary laryngology practice between February 2025 and February 2026. Demographics, prior surgical history, standardized voice measures, videostroboscopy findings. RESULTS: Fifteen adults underwent DVCT (mean age 62.8 years; 40% female). Ten had prior thyroplasty, and five had known or suspected PGI. All had abnormal acoustic and perceptual voice measures out of proportion to stroboscopy appearance. DVCT imaging findings and clinical management were analyzed. DVCT provided additional clinically relevant anatomic information beyond videostroboscopy in all patients. Imaging most commonly identified posterior glottic insufficiency, vertical height mismatch, implant malposition, or arytenoid malposition not fully appreciated on stroboscopy. CT findings influenced surgical decision-making in the majority of patients, confirming candidacy in 47%, altering planned procedures in 33%, and avoiding surgery in 13%. CONCLUSIONS: DVCT is a useful tool in the evaluation of dysphonic adults with prior laryngeal framework surgery or PGI, providing complementary characterization of glottic anatomy that informs surgical decision making.

item.title: Expression of nestin in cancer: a tissue microarray study involving 13,318 cancers from 148 tumor entities.
item.dc:creator: Schraps N, Torzewski M, von Bargen C, Gehrisch F, Menz A, Lutz F, Chirico V, Viehweger F, Dum D, Schlichter R, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Schraps N, Torzewski M, von Bargen C, Gehrisch F, Menz A, Lutz F, Chirico V, Viehweger F, Dum D, Schlichter R, et al.
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-17190-w
Published: 2026-Nov-02
PMID: 42972270



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nestin (neuroepithelial stem cell protein) is a class VI intermediate filament protein which is transiently expressed in subsets of precursor cells of various tissues during development. Nestin expression can be reinduced in the adult during pathological situations. METHODS: To better comprehend the prevalence of nestin in different cancer types, nestin was analyzed by immunohistochemistry on tissue microarrays (TMAs) containing 17,285 samples from 148 different tumor types. Our antibody was validated using a second independent antibody on 76 different normal tissues, ensuring a broad range of proteins to be tested for cross-reactivity. RESULTS: Of 13,318 analyzable tumors, nestin staining was absent in 11,677 (87.7%), weak in 961 (7.2%), moderate in 360 (2.7%), and strong in 320 (2.4%) cases. Of 148 tumor categories, 119 showed nestin staining in at least one case, and 57 included at least one sample with strong positivity. Nestin positivity was most seen in tumors of the salivary glands (up to 100%), gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (93.8%), tumors of the peripheral nerves (up to 93.8%) and malignant melanomas (81.8%). High nestin expression was linked to high grade (p < 0.0001), estrogen (p = 0.0054), and progesterone receptor negativity (p = 0.0051), as well as a triple negative phenotype (p = 0.0028) in invasive breast cancer NST, in papillary as well as poor ISUP (p=0.0149), Fuhrman (p=0.0006) and Thoenes grades (p=0.0099) in clear cell renal cell carcinoma, invasive tumor growth in urothelial carcinoma of the urinary bladder (pTa vs. pT2-4; p < 0.0001), and advanced pT stage (p = 0.0477) in serous carcinoma of the ovary. CONCLUSIONS: The data from this study provide an overview of nestin expression in human cancer and demonstrate that increased nestin levels can occur in many different tumor entities. Significant associations with unfavorable tumor characteristics in multiple entities argue for a role of nestin in driving cancer aggressiveness, which may further support the concept of exploring nestin as a drug target.

item.title: Povorcitinib for nonsegmental vitiligo: two randomized, controlled, phase 3 STOP-V trials.
item.dc:creator: Ezzedine K, Lui H, Eleftheriadou V, Desai SR, Passeron T, Ringuet J, van Geel N, Wolkerstorfer A, Lynde C, Augustin M, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Ezzedine K, Lui H, Eleftheriadou V, Desai SR, Passeron T, Ringuet J, van Geel N, Wolkerstorfer A, Lynde C, Augustin M, et al.
Journal: Nature medicine | DOI: 10.1038/s41591-026-04739-2
Published: 2026-Nov-02
PMID: 42972109



Abstract:
There is an unmet need for repigmentation therapies for patients with nonsegmental vitiligo (NSV) who are candidates for systemic therapy. Here, 52-week primary results are reported from two parallel phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of once-daily povorcitinib (oral, highly selective JAK1 inhibitor) 30 mg in adults with moderate-to-severe NSV (STOP-V1 and STOP-V2). STOP-V1 and STOP-V2 enrolled 467 and 449 patients, respectively. In both studies, the primary endpoint of ≥75% improvement in the facial Vitiligo Area Scoring Index (F-VASI75) at week 52 was met, demonstrating statistically significant and clinically meaningful repigmentation with povorcitinib versus placebo (STOP-V1: 18.9% versus 6.8%; odds ratio, 3.1; 95% confidence interval 1.6-5.9; P = 0.0003; STOP-V2: 18.9% versus 3.1%; odds ratio, 7.5; 95% confidence interval 3.0-18.6; P < 0.0001). Povorcitinib was well tolerated; the percentage of patients with any treatment-emergent adverse event (TEAE) was similar between the povorcitinib and placebo groups in both studies (STOP-V1/STOP-V2, 68.7%/66.7% versus 63.7%/62.7%). The most common TEAEs with povorcitinib were nasopharyngitis (STOP-V1/STOP-V2, 11.2%/11.3% versus placebo, 9.8%/11.1%), acne (10.7%/10.8% versus 3.0%/2.2%) and upper respiratory tract infection (6.9%/14.0% versus 9.0%/10.7%). Serious TEAEs were generally single events, and Janus kinase inhibitor class-specific TEAEs were absent or rare. These results support once-daily povorcitinib as an effective and well-tolerated systemic treatment for adults with moderate-to-severe NSV. ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers: NCT06113445 , NCT06113471 .

item.title: Efficacy of Intratympanic Sodium Thiosulfate Gel Injection to Prevent Cisplatin-Induced Ototoxicity.
item.dc:creator: Vittayakoonsakulchai K, Pitathawatchai P, Plodpai Y, Atchariyasathian V, Khaimook W, Kirtsreesakul V, Kittichet R, Prayuenyong P
item.description:
Authors: Vittayakoonsakulchai K, Pitathawatchai P, Plodpai Y, Atchariyasathian V, Khaimook W, Kirtsreesakul V, Kittichet R, Prayuenyong P
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71028
Published: 2026-Nov-02
PMID: 42971568



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of intratympanic sodium thiosulfate (STS) gel injection in preventing cisplatin-induced hearing loss. METHODS: We conducted a single-blinded randomized controlled trial, enrolling adults with head and neck cancer undergoing cisplatin chemotherapy. Intratympanic STS gel was injected into one ear within 3 h before each cisplatin cycle, while the contralateral ear served as a control. Clinical and audiometric assessments were performed before each injection and 1-3 months after the completion of chemotherapy. Changes in hearing thresholds from baseline at each frequency were measured. Ototoxicity was defined according to the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (ASHA) criteria. Adverse events associated with intratympanic STS gel injections were also monitored. RESULTS: Twenty-eight patients were included in the study. Based on ASHA criteria within the frequency range of 0.25-8 kHz, there was no statistically significant difference in the incidence of ototoxicity between the treated and control ears (p = 0.683). Compared with control ears, treated ears exhibited significantly reduced threshold shifts from baseline in the 4, 6, 8, 9, and 11 kHz, with mean differences of approximately 7-10 dB. A safety analysis of 74 injections revealed minor adverse effects, including otalgia (10.8%), transient vertigo (10.8%), dizziness (14.8%), and tympanic membrane perforation (4.0%). CONCLUSION: Our findings showed no significant difference in the incidence of cisplatin ototoxicity between STS injected and control ears. Nonetheless, intratympanic STS gel injections demonstrated potential benefits in preserving hearing at high and extended-high frequencies. The procedure was generally well-tolerated, with manageable adverse effects. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: N/A.

item.title: Androgen Receptor-Targeted Therapy for Salivary Gland Carcinoma: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.dc:creator: Rosenthal JW, Allen DZ, Sternthal J, Romeo I, Ari G, Brammer B, Reardon EE, Novaes JAMO, Saba NF, Gross J, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Rosenthal JW, Allen DZ, Sternthal J, Romeo I, Ari G, Brammer B, Reardon EE, Novaes JAMO, Saba NF, Gross J, et al.
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71034
Published: 2026-Nov-02
PMID: 42971546



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Salivary duct carcinoma (SDC) is a rare and aggressive malignancy with limited effective treatment options in the recurrent/metastatic setting. Biologically, SDC has high rates of androgen receptor (AR) expression, providing a strong rationale for AR-targeted therapy. DATA SOURCES: Ovid MEDLINE, Embase.com, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov from their inception to August 20, 2026. REVIEW METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of AR-targeted therapy in patients with AR-positive recurrent/metastatic SDC and SDC-enriched salivary gland carcinoma cohorts. The primary outcome was overall response rate (ORR). Secondary outcomes included clinical benefit rate (CBR), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS). Pooled proportions were calculated using a random-effects model. Combined androgen blockade was compared to AR-targeted monotherapy. RESULTS: Twelve studies were included in the systematic review accounting for 587 eligible patients. The primary meta-analysis has 10 eligible studies (417 patients). The pooled ORR was 26.6% (95% CI, 15.4%-42.1%). Five studies reported CBR, and the pooled CBR was 45.0% (95% CI, 38.1%-52.1%). The sample-size-weighted mean of reported median PFS was 6.3 months, and the weighted mean of reported median OS was 26.9 months among the seven studies reporting OS. ORR was higher with combined androgen blockade than with AR-targeted monotherapy (36.3% vs. 8.9%; meta-regression p = 0.023). CONCLUSION: AR-targeted therapy shows clinically meaningful activity in AR-positive disease, particularly with combined androgen blockade. The evidence remains heterogeneous and largely nonrandomized, so treatment decisions should account for HER2 status, AR expression level, treatment line, and patient tolerance.

item.title: Primary carcinoma of the lacrimal drainage system: a systematic review of treatment, outcomes and associated prognostic factors.
item.dc:creator: Bertolini M, Conti C, Caviglia A, Moro C, Fucci L, Rossi M, Iandelli A, Peretti G, Mauritz Canevari FR
item.description:
Authors: Bertolini M, Conti C, Caviglia A, Moro C, Fucci L, Rossi M, Iandelli A, Peretti G, Mauritz Canevari FR
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108198
Published: 2026-Nov-02
PMID: 42970849



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary carcinoma of the lacrimal drainage system (NLCA) is a rare and aggressive malignancy with poorly defined prognostic factors and no established treatment guidelines. OBJECTIVE: To characterize epidemiological and histopathological features, evaluate survival outcomes, and identify independent prognostic factors through a pooled analysis. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted per PRISMA guidelines. Individual patient-level data were pooled for logistic regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses. A random-effects meta-analysis of proportions was performed on aggregate data from retrospective case series. Methodological quality was assessed using JBI Critical Appraisal Checklists. RESULTS: Eighty-one studies encompassing 201 patients were included. The most frequent histologic subtype was squamous cell carcinoma (38.3 %), followed by adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC, 15.4 %). Estimated 2-year overall survival, recurrence-free survival (RFS), and metastasis-free survival (MFS) were 96 %, 88 %, and 92 %; 5-year RFS and MFS were 85 % and 91 %. ACC was independently associated with disease-related death (OR 1.79, 95 % CI 1.04-3.09, p = 0.037) and with significantly worse overall survival (log-rank p = 0.013). Positive surgical margins (R1) were associated with higher odds of recurrence (OR 8.68, 95 % CI 1.99-37.81, p = 0.004), metastasis (OR 5.05, 95 % CI 1.02-25.04, p = 0.048), and death (OR 9.62, 95 % CI 1.10-83.89, p = 0.040). Pooled recurrence, metastasis, and mortality rates were 15.0 %, 13.5 %, and 13.3 %, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory analysis, positive surgical margins and ACC histology were associated with worse oncological outcomes. Given the primary independent prognostic determinants in NLCA, R0 resection should be the principal surgical objective, while ACC warrants intensified surveillance. Multicentre prospective studies are needed to define optimal treatment algorithms.

item.title: Antithrombotic Therapy After Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: The SIMPLAAFY Randomized Clinical Trial.
item.dc:creator: Reddy VY, Saliba WI, Waggoner T, Nair DG, Weiner S, Evonich R, Hoskins M, Dublin A, Rinaldi M, Gandhi G, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Reddy VY, Saliba WI, Waggoner T, Nair DG, Weiner S, Evonich R, Hoskins M, Dublin A, Rinaldi M, Gandhi G, et al.
Journal: JAMA | DOI: 10.1001/jama.2026.21361
Published: 2026-Nov-02
PMID: 42970643



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Following a left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) procedure, antithrombotic therapy is administered to safely allow time for device endothelialization. However, the optimal postimplant antithrombotic regimen is unknown. OBJECTIVE: To determine if either reduced-dose non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants (NOACs) or aspirin alone are noninferior to dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) for the composite clinical end point of death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding through 6 months post LAAC. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This open-label, 3-group, multicenter clinical trial randomized 1857 patients between October 2024 and December 2025 at 87 US investigational sites, with the final 6-month follow-up in July 2026. Enrolled patients had nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, underwent successful LAAC, and were eligible for all 3 regimens. INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomly allocated 1:1:1 to DAPT for 6 months followed by aspirin (n = 624), a reduced-dose NOAC for 3 months followed by aspirin (n = 620), or aspirin alone for 12 months (n = 613). MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the 6-month composite of all-cause death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding. Noninferiority was tested in the primary analysis population with a 1-sided Farrington-Manning test (α = .025). Bleeding and 45-day device-related thrombus rates were exploratory without multiplicity adjustment. RESULTS: The cohort had a mean age of 76 (SD, 8) years, 42.9% were female, the mean CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4.2 (SD, 1.3), and 68.0% had paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. The primary outcome occurred in 41 patients (6.9%) with DAPT vs 31 (5.1%) with a reduced-dose NOAC (risk ratio, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.48-1.18]; risk difference, -1.7 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, 1.2) and 20 (3.3%) with aspirin alone (risk ratio, 0.49 [95% CI, 0.29-0.82]; risk difference, -3.5 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, -0.8). Both monotherapy strategies met noninferiority criteria (P < .001 for noninferiority for both). Major bleeding was 4.5% with DAPT, 2.7% with reduced-dose NOACs, and 1.7% with aspirin alone; clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was 8.7%, 4.8%, and 3.8%, respectively. Device-related thrombus was observed in 3.4%, 0.9%, and 2.7%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Both reduced-dose NOACs and aspirin alone were noninferior to DAPT for 6-month outcomes after uncomplicated LAAC. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06521463.

item.title: Erlotinib in a once-daily high-dose oral regimen could mitigate Chikungunya virus titer in mice.
item.dc:creator: Orji CN, Loeanurit N, Sroithongmoon A, Wacharachaisurapol N, Jumroen Y, Eiamart W, Wittayalertpanya S, Chaijamorn W, Sriboonruang T, Vamananda J, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Orji CN, Loeanurit N, Sroithongmoon A, Wacharachaisurapol N, Jumroen Y, Eiamart W, Wittayalertpanya S, Chaijamorn W, Sriboonruang T, Vamananda J, et al.
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360169
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42970557



Abstract:
Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a re-emerging arbovirus that causes debilitating inflammatory arthritis, for which no approved antiviral therapy currently exists. This study investigated the potential of repurposing erlotinib, a tyrosine kinase inhibitor, as an anti-CHIKV agent. Erlotinib demonstrated promising in vitro antiviral activity, with EC50 values in the low micromolar range and a favorable selectivity index. However, in vivo evaluation in C57BL/6 mice revealed pharmacokinetic limitations, characterized by rapid absorption and clearance, resulting in insufficient drug exposure under standard dosing regimens. Escalation to an intensive four-times-daily (QID) regimen successfully maintained plasma concentrations above the in vitro therapeutic threshold but led to significant body weight loss and failed to reduce viral titers or viral RNA levels in infected tissues. However, a once-daily (OD) regimen improved tolerability and significantly reduced footpad and serum viral titers relative to vehicle-treated controls. Notably, despite the lack of virological control in the QID regimen, erlotinib treatment reduced leukocyte infiltration and tissue inflammation in both treatment regimens, indicating a host-directed immunomodulatory effect. Overall, these findings highlight the critical role of dosing frequency in determining erlotinib's in vivo antiviral efficacy against CHIKV and suggest that once-daily (OD) administration may represent a more viable dosing strategy for further evaluation of erlotinib as a host-directed antiviral against CHIKV. Future strategies should also explore combination approaches with direct-acting antivirals to achieve more viral suppression and mitigation of disease pathology, as well as Structure-Activity Relationship (SAR)-guided scaffold optimization to improve in vivo pharmacokinetic profiles.

item.title: Women's experience following orthodontic treatment with conventional fixed appliances and clear aligners: A qualitative study.
item.dc:creator: San Nicolas Dubrull Lia Lucarelli N, Gonçalves Innocente G, Augusto Thiene Leme P, Paz Sampaio L, Gonzaga Gandini Junior L, Amélia Scudeler Vedovello S, Arrais Campos L, Carmo de Menezes C
item.description:
Authors: San Nicolas Dubrull Lia Lucarelli N, Gonçalves Innocente G, Augusto Thiene Leme P, Paz Sampaio L, Gonzaga Gandini Junior L, Amélia Scudeler Vedovello S, Arrais Campos L, Carmo de Menezes C
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0359709
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42970542



Abstract:
This qualitative study aimed to explore the experiences of female patients following completion of orthodontic treatment with conventional fixed appliances and clear aligners. It used a clinical qualitative design with, semi-structured interviews featuring open-ended questions. Participants were recruited from private orthodontic practices, and the sample size was determined by data saturation. The final group included six patients treated with conventional fixed appliances and nine patients treated with clear aligners. Data were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using qualitative content analysis with peer validation of the categories. Seven categories emerged among patients treated with conventional fixed appliances: pain, discomfort, and hygiene difficulties; daily adaptations and restrictions; confidence in the professional; treatment duration; insecurity or embarrassment; desire to improve appearance; and satisfaction with treatment outcomes. For patients treated with clear aligners, seven categories were identified: practicality, comfort and hygiene; pain and discomfort related to use; treatment duration; willingness to recommend aligners; desire to improve appearance and appliance discretion; recommendation by the professional; and satisfaction. The findings show that, although patients with fixed appliances faced several challenges during treatment, aesthetic improvement was the main reason for seeking care, and overall satisfaction with the results was high. Patients who chose clear aligners aimed to avoid common limitations of fixed appliances and emphasized benefits related to comfort, convenience, oral hygiene, and discretion. These results highlight the importance of qualitative methods for understanding patient perspectives and can guide clinical communication and shared decision-making in adult orthodontic treatment.

item.title: Salivary microbiome, socioeconomic status, and cognitive performance: Triangulating the relationship.
item.dc:creator: Naumova OY, Dobrynin PV, Litwin G, Rychkov SY, Milham MP, Grigorenko EL
item.description:
Authors: Naumova OY, Dobrynin PV, Litwin G, Rychkov SY, Milham MP, Grigorenko EL
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361602
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42970519



Abstract:
Research increasingly demonstrates that endogenous bacterial communities (microbiomes) are associated with both cognitive functioning and socioeconomic status (SES). In this study, we used a metagenomics approach to characterize oral microbiome diversity in Hispanic and African American children aged 6-16 years. We examined how microbiome composition and SES were related to cognitive performance, as assessed by the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children (WISC). Our findings indicate that SES and the microbiome contributed complementary, comparably sized influences on cognitive functioning. Together, variability in conventional SES indicators and microbiome composition accounted for approximately 10% of the variability in WISC scores. These results highlight the importance of integrating both social and biological determinants of health when studying cognitive performance and other psychological outcomes.

item.title: Opium Consumption and Lung Cancer: From Self-reported Use to Exposure Biomarkers.
item.dc:creator: Leng S
item.description:
Authors: Leng S
Journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology | DOI: 10.1158/1055-9965.EPI-26-1173
Published: 2026-Nov-02
PMID: 42968657



Abstract:
Opium consumption is most prevalent in Southwestern and South Asia, particularly in regions surrounding the major opium-producing areas of the Golden Crescent. The International Agency for Research on Cancer classifies opium consumption as a group 1 human carcinogen, with sufficient evidence for lung, laryngeal, and urinary bladder cancers. Opium consumption involves complex exposure profiles, including combustion-derived exposures from opium and its fuels, as well as coexposures from tobacco smoking and indoor biomass burning. Recent molecular epidemiologic research in the prospective Golestan Cohort Study provides an opportunity to move beyond self-reported opium use by characterizing internal exposure to multiple opioid and non-opioid constituents. In a nested case-control study of 53 matched lung cancer pairs among opium users, 35 urinary metabolites reflecting exposure to opiates, volatile organic compounds, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, and nicotine were measured. Higher concentrations of morphine-3-glucuronide, morphine-6-glucuronide, 2-hydroxypropyl mercapturic acid, and 2-hydroxyethyl mercapturic acid were associated with lung cancer. These findings provide an important initial demonstration of the potential of urinary biomarkers to characterize complex exposures associated with opium consumption. Future studies integrating driver mutations, mutational signatures, and tumor microenvironment characteristics may provide further insight into mechanisms of opium-related lung carcinogenesis and inform cancer prevention and precision oncology. See related article by Naghash et al., p. 1880.

item.title: Association of HPV Status With Quality of Life After Transoral Robotic Surgery for T1-T2 Oropharyngeal Carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Tesauro P, Khalaf M, Breuskin I, Mercante G, Temam S, Gorphe P
item.description:
Authors: Tesauro P, Khalaf M, Breuskin I, Mercante G, Temam S, Gorphe P
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70540
Published: 2026-Nov-01
PMID: 42968417



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In T1-T2 oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), factors associated with patient-reported quality of life after transoral robotic surgery (TORS) are poorly defined. METHODS: Retrospective cohort of 59 patients with T1-T2 OPSCC treated with TORS. Swallowing-related quality of life (MD Anderson Dysphagia Inventory, MDADI) and EORTC QLQ-C30/QLQ-H&N35 scores were analyzed with mixed-effects models adjusted for HPV status, subsite, adjuvant treatment and, in sensitivity analyses, lifestyle factors, age, tumor stage, and preoperative scores. RESULTS: HPV-positive status was independently associated with higher MDADI scores (β = 12.39, p = 0.001), including after adjustment for preoperative scores (β = 16.0, p = 0.004), and with lower QLQ-H&N35 symptom burden (β = -9.5, p = 0.012). Adjuvant radiotherapy was associated with lower MDADI scores (β = -7.92, p = 0.021), attenuated after adjustment for tumor stage. Tumor subsite was not associated with outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: HPV-positive patients report better swallowing-related quality of life after TORS, independently of preoperative scores.

item.title: Development and Internal Validation of a Competing-Risk Nomogram for Predicting Cancer-Specific Death in Oral Cavity Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Chu KY
item.description:
Authors: Chu KY
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70556
Published: 2026-Nov-01
PMID: 42968192



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC) patients face competing risks of cancer and non-cancer death. This study developed and internally validated a competing-risk nomogram for cancer-specific death. METHODS: A total of 84,456 SEER 17-registry adults (age ≥ 20 years) with OCSCC (2000-2023) were identified. A Fine-Gray model was fit on a 70% training split, with backward elimination of nine candidate predictors (gender retained a priori). The nomogram, predicting 3- and 5-year cancer-specific death, was evaluated on the 30% test set against a stage-only benchmark, with Cox sensitivity analyses. RESULTS: The final model retained age, race, subsite, grade, stage, surgery, radiation and gender. Distant (vs. localized) stage (sHR 3.48, 95% CI: 3.30-3.66) and surgery (sHR 0.48, 95% CI: 0.46-0.50) were the strongest predictors. Time-dependent AUC was 0.777 (3-year) and 0.765 (5-year), 5-6 points above the stage-only model (p < 0.001), with good calibration and Brier scores better than a null model (p < 0.001). Proportional-hazards assumptions were violated (p < 0.001), so estimates are time-averaged; radiation's estimated direction differed between Fine-Gray and Cox models, likely reflecting confounding by indication. CONCLUSION: This competing-risk nomogram provides individualized, reasonably well-calibrated 3- and 5-year cancer-specific death risk estimates for OCSCC. External validation is needed before clinical use.

item.title: Delays in Diagnosis in Primary and Secondary Care in Oral Cancer Patients: A Critical Review.

PMID: 42967973



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Earlier diagnosis of cancers and timely treatment are associated with improved survival. In oral cancer, however, the true impact of diagnostic delays on clinical outcomes remains insufficiently understood. AIM: To perform a structured narrative review to assess the impact of delays experienced by oral cancer patients during the primary and secondary care intervals. METHODS: A systematic search was undertaken in PubMed, EMBASE, SciELO, and Scopus databases since year 2000. The study followed the PRISMA guidelines. RESULTS: The 18 studies were included; seven on Primary Care delays and 11 on Secondary Care intervals, with data from 76,954 patients. Heterogeneous definitions, arbitrary time thresholds, and diverse assessment criteria were found to describe time intervals. Up to 9.5% of patients had primary professional delay. Inaccurate treatments received in primary settings were removal of teeth (24%) and prescribing topical preparations (20%). Delays exceeding 30 days in secondary care were consistently associated with adverse survival outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: The Primary and Secondary Care intervals are measurable and modifiable components of diagnostic delay in patients with oral cancer. However, conceptual heterogeneity and limited adherence to the published guidelines restrict the ability to draw conclusions regarding the impact of these intervals on diagnostic delay and survival outcomes in oral cancer patients.

item.title: Salivary Metabolomic Alterations in Primary Sjögren Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.dc:creator: Amalina FI, Nazar NSM, Dharmarajan L, Jacob PS, Munusamy SM, Mohamed RJBR, Zain RB, Al-Maleki ARM, Ramanathan A
item.description:
Authors: Amalina FI, Nazar NSM, Dharmarajan L, Jacob PS, Munusamy SM, Mohamed RJBR, Zain RB, Al-Maleki ARM, Ramanathan A
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70561
Published: 2026-Nov-01
PMID: 42967899



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This systematic review assesses the diagnostic potential of salivary metabolomics in discriminating between primary Sjögren disease (pSjD) and healthy controls, aiming to identify potential biomarkers for clinical application. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Web of Science and Scopus following the Centre for Reviews and Dissemination and PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Methodological quality was primarily assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy in OMICS (QUADOMICS) tool. Meta-analysis utilised random-effects models, with effect sizes presented via forest plots. RESULTS: Nine studies met criteria, displaying heterogeneous metabolite profiles. Meta-analysis of two studies with complete quantitative data revealed no significant differences in glycine, pyruvic acid or succinic acid levels between pSjD and controls. Glycine demonstrated substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 81.2%), whereas pyruvic and succinic acids showed consistent pooled effects with no heterogeneity (I2 = 0%). CONCLUSIONS: Evidence for succinic acid, pyruvic acid and glycine as salivary biomarkers remains insufficient. Although pSjD is associated with alterations in the salivary metabolome, the evidence remains limited and heterogeneous. Further high-quality studies are required to clarify their diagnostic potential. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: pSjD saliva exhibits a metabolic 'shift', suggesting that salivary metabolomics may reflect disease-related alterations despite variability in individual metabolites.

item.title: Parathyroid Hormone for Medication-Related Osteonecrosis of the Jaw: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.dc:creator: Alabdulaaly L, Alfadhel AA, Juwaid AZB, Almazyad A
item.description:
Authors: Alabdulaaly L, Alfadhel AA, Juwaid AZB, Almazyad A
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70551
Published: 2026-Nov-01
PMID: 42967897



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) is a complication of antiresorptive therapy and can be refractory to treatment. Teriparatide (TPTD) has shown promise in the management of MRONJ. We aimed to comprehensively evaluate the impact of TPTD on MRONJ prevention and healing. METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Ovid, and LILACS in December 2024 to include studies that utilized TPTD/abaloparatide MRONJ management or prevention. Correlation analysis, meta-analysis, and meta-regression analysis were conducted. Quality assessment was performed using the Joanna Briggs Institute tool. RESULTS: All studies used TPTD for MRONJ management. Twenty-eight studies with 278 participants were included (TPTD n = 161; non-TPTD n = 117). MRONJ improvement was noted in 90.1% of the TPTD-treated group and 81.2% in the non-TPTD-treated group (odds ratio 5.81). The highest resolution rates were observed among patients who received a combination of surgical and non-surgical interventions for MRONJ in both groups. CONCLUSIONS: Our results suggest a possible positive effect of TPTD on MRONJ resolution, and TPTD may have a synergistic effect when combined with surgical and non-surgical interventions. These results must be interpreted with caution since analyses were based on publications with a small number of cases and with variable outcome assessment reporting.

item.title: Prevention of Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders and Career Sustainability in Head and Neck Reconstructive Surgery: Integrating Ergonomics and Physical Conditioning.
item.dc:creator: Shadgan B, Butskiy O, Apostolopoulos NC, Sarkissian L, Chang B, Anderson D
item.description:
Authors: Shadgan B, Butskiy O, Apostolopoulos NC, Sarkissian L, Chang B, Anderson D
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70539
Published: 2026-Nov-01
PMID: 42967822



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Head and neck reconstructive and plastic surgery exposes surgeons to prolonged static posture, sustained visualization of a narrow operative field, cervical and shoulder loading, fine-motor work, and extended standing. These demands create a substantial occupational musculoskeletal burden. METHODS: A structured narrative review and expert perspective synthesized evidence from head and neck surgery, reconstructive microsurgery, plastic surgery, surgical ergonomics, occupational health, and rehabilitation. RESULTS: Musculoskeletal symptoms commonly involve the neck, shoulders, back, and upper extremities and often begin during residency. Exposure varies by operative phase, visualization, anthropometric and team-level mismatch, prolonged standing, and repetitive operative workload. Prevention extends beyond ergonomic setup to phase-specific exposure modification, physical conditioning, mobility and recovery, footwear and standing-surface optimization, wearable feedback, early assessment, and diagnosis-specific rehabilitation. CONCLUSIONS: Career sustainability requires reducing avoidable occupational load while preserving physical capacity and restoring function through recognition, modification, conditioning, recovery, assessment, and rehabilitation.

item.title: A prospective randomized evaluation of AI assisted GTV contouring in head-and-neck radiotherapy.
item.dc:creator: Rasmussen ME, Ren J, Nijkamp JA, Holm AIS, Moos K, Hochreuter KM, Primdahl H, Andreassen CN, Toustrup K, Schack LMH, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Rasmussen ME, Ren J, Nijkamp JA, Holm AIS, Moos K, Hochreuter KM, Primdahl H, Andreassen CN, Toustrup K, Schack LMH, et al.
Journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.radonc.2026.111854
Published: 2026-Nov-01
PMID: 42967540



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: AI-assisted contouring has demonstrated efficiency and consistency benefits for organs-at-risk in radiotherapy. However, its impact on gross tumor volume (GTV) delineation remains unexplored. The aim of this study was to evaluate AI-assisted GTV contouring in head and neck cancer radiotherapy in an exploratory randomized controlled clinical trial. METHODS: In this prospective, single-centre, randomized controlled evaluation, patients referred for curative-intent radiotherapy of head-neck cancer were randomized to manual contouring (control) or AI-assisted contouring (intervention) of gross tumor volumes using an in-house developed segmentation model. The primary endpoint was the extent of editing during a blinded multidisciplinary target conference, using normalized Added Path Length (APL). Secondary endpoints included conference duration, self-reported contouring time, and perceived complexity of the cases. RESULTS: Between Sept 11, 2023, and Jan 20, 2025, 85 patients were enrolled; 83 were included in the analysis (41 control, 42 AI-assisted). The median difference in APL (AI-assisted minus control, negative favoring the intervention) was -0.02 [-0.32; 0.07] for GTV-T and 0.06 [-0.01; 0.14] for GTV-N. Conference duration, contouring time, and perceived complexity were similar between groups. No adverse events were reported. CONCLUSION: The median difference in APL between groups was consistent with no relevant effect for GTV-T. For GTV-N, however, AI-assisted contouring tended towards more editing during peer review for APL, but not for supplementary contour metrics. No efficiency benefits were demonstrated. Overall, these findings do not indicate a concern, but warrants further research before widespread adoption.

item.title: Real world clinical outcomes of deep learning based versus manual proton therapy planning for oropharyngeal cancer: A matched cohort study.
item.dc:creator: van Bruggen IG, van der Laan HP, Hessels AC, Steenbakkers RJHM, van den Hoek JGM, Oldehinkel E, Verbeek HHG, Atasoyu M, Brinkman-Akker MJ, Korevaar EW, et al.
item.description:
Authors: van Bruggen IG, van der Laan HP, Hessels AC, Steenbakkers RJHM, van den Hoek JGM, Oldehinkel E, Verbeek HHG, Atasoyu M, Brinkman-Akker MJ, Korevaar EW, et al.
Journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.radonc.2026.111856
Published: 2026-Nov-01
PMID: 42967539



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Recent deep learning (DL)-based planning approaches to intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) have shown promise for improving planning efficiency and quality. A recent study demonstrated clinical acceptable DL-based plan quality in patients with oropharyngeal cancer (OPC), this study used real-world clinical outcomes to compare oncological outcomes acute and early late side effects between OPC patients treated with DL-based IMPT and those treated with manual planning. METHODS: In this observational matched cohort study, OPC patients were treated with DL-based IMPT, and were matched 1:1 to a recent manually planned IMPT cohort (74 vs 74). In DL-based planning, U-Net predicted dose distributions were robustly optimized and manually refined for approximately two hours. Overall survival, progression-free survival, locoregional control, and distant metastasis-free survival were evaluated using survival analysis. Acute and early late side effects were prospectively assessed according to CTCAE v4.0 and patient-rated symptoms were scored using the EORTC QLQH&N35 questionnaire at baseline, weekly during treatment, 12 weeks, 6 months and 12 months after treatment start. The impact of the planning method was evaluated using generalized estimating equations adjusted for baseline values. RESULTS: No statistically significant differences were observed for any oncological outcome. Similarly, no statistically significant differences in acute and early late side effects were observed between DL-based and manual planning. CONCLUSION: In real-world clinical practice, the findings of this study provide no evidence that DL-based IMPT is associated with different oncological outcomes or side effects than manual planning. These findings support the clinical implementation of DL-based planning in patients with OPC.

item.title: A multicenter, prospective, phase 2 trial on proton re-irradiation for patients with previously treated head and neck cancer.
item.dc:creator: Dee EC, Barker CA, Kalman NS, Wu Y, White C, Zhang Z, Lin H, Gelblum DY, Yu Y, Kang JJ, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Dee EC, Barker CA, Kalman NS, Wu Y, White C, Zhang Z, Lin H, Gelblum DY, Yu Y, Kang JJ, et al.
Journal: Cancer | DOI: 10.1002/cncr.70643
Published: 2026-Nov-01
PMID: 42963935



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Re-irradiation (re-RT) for recurrent head and neck cancer (HNC) can be potentially curative but is constrained by significant toxicity. Proton therapy may improve the therapeutic ratio. This multicenter phase 2 trial evaluated the safety and efficacy of proton re-RT in patients with HNC. METHODS: Patients received prior HNC radiotherapy at a dose of ≥40 gray (Gy). Salvage surgery and/or systemic therapy before re-RT were permitted. Considering clinical status, two pragmatic treatment approaches were used: fractionated re-RT (F-Re-RT; 60-70 Gy) or QUAD shot re-RT (QS-Re-RT; 14.8 Gy per cycle, up to four cycles; maximum total, 59.2 Gy). Primary end points were locoregional recurrence-free rates at 12 months for F-Re-RT and at 6 months for QS-Re-RT, and a fixed-time, binary proportion analyzed using 90% Clopper-Pearson confidence intervals (CIs) and prespecified success thresholds (lower bound, >55% and >10%, respectively). Secondary end points included overall survival (OS), progression-free survival, the cumulative incidence of distant metastasis and locoregional recurrence, clinician-reported toxicity, and patient-reported outcomes. RESULTS: From July 2017 to November 2022, 85 patients received either F-Re-RT (n = 57) or QS-Re-RT (n = 28), with a median follow-up of 38 months. The locoregional recurrence-free rates were 71% (90% CI, 59%-81%) at 12 months for F-Re-RT and 76% (90% CI, 58%-89%) at 6 months for QS-Re-RT, surpassing prespecified success thresholds. The highest late toxicity attributable to re-RT was grade 3 in 20% of patients, grade 4 in 11%, and grade 5 in 4%. The 5-year OS rate was 29%, and the 5-year progression-free survival rate was 23%. Patient-reported outcomes were stable at 1 year after F-Re-RT and after QS-Re-RT. CONCLUSIONS: Proton re-RT demonstrated encouraging locoregional control and survival in heavily pretreated patients, although late toxicities remain important concerns (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03217188).

item.title: Improving outcomes in the management of acute external laryngotracheal trauma.
item.dc:creator: Mathews SS, Sargunaraj JJE, Chetan SM, Boaz RT, Paul RR, Gurushekar PR, Karuppusami R, Albert RRA
item.description:
Authors: Mathews SS, Sargunaraj JJE, Chetan SM, Boaz RT, Paul RR, Gurushekar PR, Karuppusami R, Albert RRA
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10783-y
Published: 2026-Oct-31
PMID: 42966818



Abstract:
AIMS AND OBJECTIVES: To highlight the presentation, management, and functional outcomes of subjects with acute laryngotracheal trauma, managed by a dedicated laryngology unit in a tertiary care hospital in South India. METHODS: A retrospective review of the medical records of acute laryngotracheal trauma cases from 1st January 2014 to 31st August 2023 was carried out. Data collected included demographics, mechanism of trauma, age, and sex, presentation, time of injury to intervention, investigations, Schaefer-Fuhrman (SF) grade, management (airway access, surgical techniques & conservative methods) and outcomes. Complications (via a graded complication classification grouped into mild, moderate , severe), functional airway, voice and swallowing outcomes were analysed separately as well as at the end of one year follow up. RESULTS: Sixty-eight subjects (57 males and 11 females) with laryngotracheal trauma were managed during this study period. All but 2 subjects received definitive management within 48 hours of the trauma. 91.2% (n=62) of them were managed within 24 hours of the injury. We encountered 2 deaths and one subject developed Hypoxic Ischaemic encephalopathy (HIE) during emergent management. Main mode of injury was motor vehicular accident (41%, n=28). SF group III and IV was observed in 33.8% (n=23) and 29.4% (n=20) subjects. The endolaryngeal mucosal repair as well as reduction and stabilisation of fractured cartilage segments were done using absorbable polyglactin (vicryl). Of the 54 who required surgery only 16 % (n=11) required stenting. Successful decannulation was achieved in 96% of the tracheostomised subjects (n=48/50) and successful rehabilitation from assisted to oral feeding was possible in 90.7 % (n=39/43). Poor voice, airway and swallowing outcomes were seen in 11%, 3% and 3% of our subjects during 1 year follow up. Long -term major complications were seen in 6% (n=4) and minor ones in 15.4 % (n=10). CONCLUSION: Early intervention remains pivotal for successful management of laryngotracheal trauma. This single institutional study, characterized primarily by early definitive management by an experienced team; was able to achieve favourable outcomes even with the use of simple, readily available, inexpensive materials like - absorbable sutures for mucosal and cartilage approximation, and modified endotracheal tube as stents.

item.title: Prolonged hospitalization following head and neck cancer surgery: risk factors, clinical outcomes, and strategies for care optimization.
item.dc:creator: Kim Y, Woo SY, Cho H, Choi SM, Ha J, Kim EH, Jeong HS
item.description:
Authors: Kim Y, Woo SY, Cho H, Choi SM, Ha J, Kim EH, Jeong HS
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10736-5
Published: 2026-Oct-31
PMID: 42966811



Abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to identify risk factors for prolonged hospital length of stay (LOS) following head and neck cancer (HNC) surgery, evaluate its oncologic impact, and identify clinically actionable targets to reduce LOS. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed a 10-year cohort of HNC patients treated surgically at a tertiary referral center (2013-2022). Prolonged LOS was defined as hospitalization exceeding the 95th percentile (> 24 days) and extremely prolonged LOS as exceeding the 99th percentile (> 73 days); patients with a mean LOS of 10 days served as controls. Risk factors were assessed using multivariable logistic regression, and quantile regression and network analyses evaluated the relative importance and interrelationships of postoperative complications. RESULTS: Of 365 patients, 44 had extremely prolonged LOS, 182 had prolonged LOS, and 139 were controls. Prolonged LOS was associated with more complications and poorer oncologic outcomes, including higher recurrence and disease-specific mortality. Laryngeal/hypopharyngeal subsite (odds ratio [OR], 4.95, 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.13-23.69), previous surgery (OR, 10.60, 95% CI, 3.81-35.79), smoking (OR, 0.26, 95% CI, 0.07-0.93), tracheostomy (OR, 3.62, 95% CI, 1.16-12.16), and postoperative complications (OR, 251.2, 95% CI, 29.9-33,729.2) were significant baseline or postoperative correlates of prolonged LOS. Flap failure was the most influential complication, and network analysis revealed strong interrelationships among flap failure, fistula, wound necrosis, and infection. CONCLUSION: Prolonged hospitalization after HNC surgery is associated with adverse oncologic outcomes which may reflect underlying disease severity, and is primarily driven by postoperative complications, particularly flap-related complications, the most important and modifiable determinant of prolonged LOS.

item.title: Clinical characteristics, management, and long-term outcomes of nasopharyngeal osteoradionecrosis after radiotherapy for nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a single-institution experience.
item.dc:creator: Hwang J, Lee DH, Lim SC
item.description:
Authors: Hwang J, Lee DH, Lim SC
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10748-1
Published: 2026-Oct-31
PMID: 42966810



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nasopharyngeal osteoradionecrosis (ORN) is an uncommon but serious late complication after radiotherapy for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). This study aimed to characterize the clinical features, management strategies, and long-term outcomes of nasopharyngeal ORN treated at a single institution. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients with NPC who underwent radiotherapy at our institution and identified those who subsequently developed nasopharyngeal ORN. Demographic data, radiation-related factors, presenting symptoms, endoscopic and radiologic findings, treatment modalities, and oncologic and functional outcomes were analyzed. Particular attention was given to the role of endoscopic debridement and nasoseptal flap (NSF) reconstruction. RESULTS: Among 325 patients with NPC treated with radiotherapy, 13 developed nasopharyngeal ORN, corresponding to an observed frequency of 4.0%. This study highlights the rarity of this condition and provides extended longitudinal data, with a median follow-up of 105 months. Clinical presentation and disease extent varied, and treatment was individualized according to necrotic burden and tissue status. Endoscopic debridement was used as a surgical management option, and NSF reconstruction was feasible for providing vascularized wound coverage in selected patients. Long-term follow-up demonstrated meaningful information regarding disease control, treatment response, and late outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: Nasopharyngeal ORN after radiotherapy for NPC is a rare but clinically significant entity. Endoscopic debridement may be considered when clinically indicated, and selective NSF reconstruction may represent a feasible reconstructive option in appropriately selected patients. This single-institution experience adds long-term outcome data that may help guide diagnosis, treatment planning, and surveillance in affected patients.

item.title: Epidemiology of oropharyngeal carcinoma in Europe: human papilloma virus contribution, incidence and mortality rates.
item.dc:creator: Sampieri C, Rojas-Lechuga MJ, Vilaseca I, De Virgilio A, Avilés-Jurado FX, Ferreli F, Spriano G, Costantino A
item.description:
Authors: Sampieri C, Rojas-Lechuga MJ, Vilaseca I, De Virgilio A, Avilés-Jurado FX, Ferreli F, Spriano G, Costantino A
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10782-z
Published: 2026-Oct-31
PMID: 42966809



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Oropharyngeal cancer (OPC) has emerged as a growing public health concern, primarily driven by the increasing incidence of human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated cases. This study aims to provide a comprehensive epidemiological overview of OPC in Europe, including incidence, mortality, and HPV-related burden. METHODS: We analyzed publicly available cancer registry data from 29 European countries. Age-standardized incidence and death rates (ASIR and ASDR) were calculated using the WHO World Standard Population. Temporal trends between 2000 and 2024 were analyzed using annual percentage change (APC) estimated by log-linear regression of registry-based incidence rates. A systematic literature review was conducted to determine the HPV-attributable fraction (AF) of OPC by country. RESULTS: In 2024, 22,063 new OPC cases were reported in Europe (mean ASIR: 2.10 per 100,000), with marked geographic variability. Incidence was higher among males (3.51) than females (0.80), and APCs showed the most rapid significant increases in Ireland, the UK and Denmark. The overall HPV-attributable fraction was 43.3%, ranging from 20.2% in Slovenia to 71.7% in Sweden. Mortality remained elevated in several Eastern European countries. CONCLUSION: OPC incidence continues to rise across Europe, with significant inter-country differences and a growing role of HPV. These findings underscore the need for country-specific policies of expanded HPV vaccination, enhanced surveillance, and age-adapted preventive strategies to mitigate the rising OPC burden.

item.title: Health technology assessment of robotic tonsillectomy for benign disease: clinical outcomes and economic evaluation in a retrospective cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Guillén Martínez AJ, Pérez Coll ÁO, Costa Jiménez R, Molina Moreno A, Sevilla Heras E, García-Purriños García FJ
item.description:
Authors: Guillén Martínez AJ, Pérez Coll ÁO, Costa Jiménez R, Molina Moreno A, Sevilla Heras E, García-Purriños García FJ
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10767-y
Published: 2026-Oct-31
PMID: 42966805



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Robotic-assisted surgery has an established role in oropharyngeal malignancy, but its value in benign tonsillar disease remains unexplored. This study compared clinical outcomes and direct healthcare costs between robotic-assisted and conventional electrocautery tonsillectomy in adults with benign tonsillar disease. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 60 consecutive adult patients undergoing bilateral tonsillectomy (30 robotic, 30 conventional electrocautery) at a tertiary referral hospital in Spain between April and December 2025. The primary outcome was postoperative haemorrhage requiring hospital assessment or admission. An economic evaluation, including an opportunity-cost analysis, was conducted from the perspective of the public healthcare system. RESULTS: Patients undergoing robotic surgery were significantly younger (24.2 vs. 36.8 years; p = 0.005). Postoperative haemorrhage was significantly more frequent after robotic tonsillectomy (30.0% vs. 6.7%; relative risk 4.50, 95% CI 1.06-19.11; p = 0.042) and remained independently associated with robotic surgery on multivariable analysis (adjusted OR 6.39, 95% CI 1.04-39.21; p = 0.045). Robotic surgery was also associated with longer hospital stay (3.27 vs. 1.41 days; p = 0.007) and higher readmission rates (50.0% vs. 16.7%; p = 0.013). Mean direct hospital cost was substantially higher with robotic surgery (€8,290.30 vs. €3,175.03 per patient; p < 0.001), representing a dominated healthcare technology with considerable opportunity costs. CONCLUSION: Robotic-assisted tonsillectomy for benign disease was associated with worse clinical outcomes and substantially higher costs than conventional electrocautery tonsillectomy, and its routine implementation cannot currently be recommended.

item.title: Buying Protection from Hypoparathyroidism: Is High-Tech Parathyroid Identification During Thyroidectomy Worth the Cost?
item.dc:creator: Zhang D, Brucchi F, Colombo C, Barbieri D, Dionigi G
item.description:
Authors: Zhang D, Brucchi F, Colombo C, Barbieri D, Dionigi G
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10765-0
Published: 2026-Oct-31
PMID: 42966804



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypoparathyroidism remains a major complication of total thyroidectomy, with long-term morbidity and substantial healthcare costs. Multiple intraoperative technologies have been introduced to improve parathyroid identification, but their comparative economic value and optimal use across settings are uncertain. METHODS: A decision-analytic study was conducted using a decision tree linked to a state-transition micro-costing model to simulate 1,000 adults undergoing total thyroidectomy, 70% without and 30% with central neck dissection. Analyses were performed from the hospital provider perspective under standardised calcium-parathyroid hormone pathways. Nine strategies were compared: visual inspection, magnifying loupes, methylene blue, ultrasound mapping, intraoperative intact parathyroid hormone measurement, camera-based near-infrared autofluorescence (camera-based NIRAF), camera-based NIRAF with or without indocyanine green (ICG), probe-based NIRAF (PTeye), and carbon nanoparticles. Primary outcomes were rates of transient and permanent hypoparathyroidism, total costs per patient, and incremental cost-effectiveness ratios, evaluated at 12 months and over 10 years with 3% annual discounting. Deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses (10,000 simulations) explored parameter and structural uncertainty. The model was intended as a decision-support framework for institutions considering adoption, identifying the case-volume, baseline-risk and cost conditions under which added intraoperative costs could be offset. RESULTS: With visual identification alone, simulated 12‑month rates of transient and permanent hypoparathyroidism were 27.5% and 3.8% in high-volume centres and 34.2% and 5.6% in low-volume centres. Applying literature-derived relative risks, camera-based NIRAF was associated with lower modelled rates of transient hypoparathyroidism (16.8%-20.5%), an effect supported by randomised and meta-analytic evidence, and with smaller modelled reductions in permanent hypoparathyroidism (1.6%-2.4%), for which clinical evidence remains uncertain. In patients undergoing central neck dissection, camera-based NIRAF plus ICG was associated with lower modelled transient (21.7% vs. 42.3%) and permanent hypoparathyroidism (2.8% vs. 7.9%). At 12 months, modelled mean costs with camera-based NIRAF were €160-€270 lower per patient, and €590 lower in high-risk cases with central compartment lymph node dissection. Over 10 years, under the base-case assumption of a modest reduction in permanent hypoparathyroidism, camera-based NIRAF was frequently cost-saving and had the highest probability of being cost-effective. In a prespecified scenario assuming no reduction in permanent hypoparathyroidism, camera-based NIRAF was only marginally cost-saving at 12 months and was no longer clearly dominant over 10 years, indicating that its long-term economic advantage depends substantially on the assumed permanent-hypoparathyroidism benefit. CONCLUSIONS: In this model-based economic evaluation, camera-based NIRAF-guided parathyroid identification showed favourable modelled cost profiles, particularly in high-volume and high-risk thyroid surgery. Modelled reductions in transient hypocalcaemia were supported by comparatively robust evidence, whereas reductions in permanent hypoparathyroidism, and the associated long-term savings, were more uncertain and should be regarded as model-based projections rather than established clinical expectations. The projected economic benefits are consequences of assumed clinical effects and do not constitute additional evidence of clinical efficacy. Because all costs were derived from a single healthcare system, the absolute costs, incremental cost-effectiveness ratios, and cost-saving thresholds require local recalibration before informing procurement or policy decisions in other settings. Rather than supporting a specific adoption strategy, these findings identify the conditions under which camera-based NIRAF could provide economic value (higher baseline risk, sufficient case volume, and a genuine effect on permanent hypoparathyroidism), and should be confirmed in prospective comparative studies.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: To examine racial disparities in conditional survival (CS) among patients with oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). Abstract:

Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Retrosternal goiter (RSG) remains one of the most challenging conditions in thyroid surgery because of its variable mediastinal extension, close relationship with vital mediastinal structures, and occasional need for extracervical surgical approaches. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed including consecutive patients who underwent surgery for retrosternal goiter at Erciyes University Faculty of Medicine between January 2012 and June 2025. Cervical swelling was the most common presenting symptom, while nearly one-third of patients were diagnosed incidentally. 91% of patients were euthyroid preoperatively. Total thyroidectomy was the predominant surgical procedure. Abstract:

The observed trends reflect Seychelles' epidemiological transition, with a shift from infection-related cancers towards cancers associated with ageing and lifestyle factors, resembling the cancer profile of high-income countries. Nevertheless, the major cancers-prostate, breast, colorectal, and cervical-continue to be diagnosed at relatively advanced stages, highlighting the need for improved early detection and timely diagnosis.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the operative setup, safety principles, and stepwise technique for laser-assisted transoral robotic supraglottic laryngectomy using a flexible CO2 laser system. METHODS: This operative video demonstrates laser-assisted transoral robotic supraglottic laryngectomy performed with the da Vinci SP platform. Key technical steps include laser-safe airway management, transoral exposure with a Feyh-Kastenbauer retractor, robotic docking, flexible CO2 laser fiber placement through a distal drop-in guide, aiming-beam confirmation, noncontact laser dissection, coordinated bedside suction and bipolar hemostasis, and en bloc specimen delivery. RESULTS: The technique allows controlled transoral access to the supraglottic larynx with three-dimensional visualization, precise noncontact laser incision, and preservation of uninvolved glottic and subglottic structures. A deliberate sequence of inferior, lateral, and superior release facilitates exposure of the pre-epiglottic space, specimen mobilization, and margin-oriented en bloc resection. CONCLUSION: Laser-assisted transoral robotic supraglottic laryngectomy combines the precision of CO2 laser surgery with the visualization and dexterity of single-port robotic surgery. item.title: Geographical Location and Response to Trismus Rehabilitation Following Head and Neck Cancer Treatment: A Secondary Analysis of the Restorabite Trials.

Authors: Ricketts V, Charters E, Frowen J, Poke S, Gleeson S, Pryor L, Heng C, Adshead B, Lai M, Boehm J, et al.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trismus is a common and disabling complication following head and neck cancer (HNC) treatment, particularly after multimodal therapy. Survivors in regional areas face barriers to accessing specialist rehabilitation. This study explored whether a patient's geographical location of residence influenced their response to trismus therapy. METHODS: Secondary analysis of pooled data from three Restorabite trials (2021-2024) was performed. Adults with HNC-related trismus (maximal interincisal opening [MIO] ≤ 35 mm) completed a 10-week individualized rehabilitation program incorporating manual therapy, daily jaw exercises, and weekly speech pathology review delivered in person or via telehealth. Most participants (96.6%) received all or part of their intervention via telehealth. Outcomes included MIO and Gothenburg Trismus Questionnaire (GTQ) scores. Longitudinal change was modeled using generalized estimating equations. RESULTS: A total of 175 participants with a broad range of HNC subsites, tumor stage, and treatment modalities were included. MIO improved by an average of 1.2 mm/week and GTQ scores by -2.7 points/week after 10 weeks of trismus rehabilitation (both p < 0.001). While multimodal treatment had a negative effect on both MIO and GTQ, geographical residence was not associated with change in MIO or GTQ in adjusted models (p = 0.5 and p = 0.1, respectively). CONCLUSIONS: For geographically dispersed patients, geographical residence was not associated with poorer trismus outcomes within a predominantly telehealth-supported model of care, supporting the use of telehealth to facilitate access to specialist trismus rehabilitation.

item.title: Factors for Favorable Outcomes After Sialendoscopy for Radioactive Iodine-Induced Sialadenitis of Parotid Gland: An Exploratory Study Toward a Phenotypic Patterns.

Authors: Kim S, Park MJ, Kim JW
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70527

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radioactive iodine (RAI) therapy can induce radioactive iodine-induced sialadenitis (RAIS). Sialendoscopy is an effective treatment for RAIS, but predictors of favorable outcomes remain poorly defined. This study aimed to identify functional and anatomical factors associated with favorable outcomes following sialendoscopy in RAIS patients. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 44 cases who underwent sialendoscopy for RAIS. Favorable outcome was defined as a symptom resolution without the need for additional medication or revision surgery. RESULTS: In the multivariate model, ΔSFR(pre) (difference between stimulated and unstimulated preoperative SFR) (p = 0.035), symptom duration (p = 0.039), and distal stenosis (p = 0.024) were confirmed as predictors. ROC curve analysis determined the optimal cutoffs for the two continuous independent predictors: low ΔSFR(pre) < 0.41, early intervention < 4.5 months. CONCLUSIONS: This study identified low ΔSFR(pre), early intervention, and distal stenosis of Stenson's duct as associated with favorable outcome.

item.title: Comparison of HPV Antibodies Measured Prior to Diagnosis of Anal, Cervical, Oropharyngeal, Penile and Vaginal Cancers in the HPV Cancer Cohort Consortium.
item.dc:creator: Onwuka JU, Nobels MP, Kreimer AR, Schroeder L, Ferreiro-Iglesias A, Agalliu I, Albanes D, Cai Q, D'Souza G, Freedman ND, et al.

Authors: Onwuka JU, Nobels MP, Kreimer AR, Schroeder L, Ferreiro-Iglesias A, Agalliu I, Albanes D, Cai Q, D'Souza G, Freedman ND, et al.
Journal: International journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1002/ijc.70786
Published: 2026-Oct-30
PMID: 42963861



Abstract:
Antibodies against HPV proteins can provide pre-diagnostic information about cancer development. We described the prevalence of antibodies to proteins of oncogenic HPV types prior to diagnosis of HPV-related cancers. We analysed pre-diagnostic blood from 1700 participants with incident HPV-related cancers (anal = 387, cervical = 274, oropharyngeal = 788, penile = 168, vaginal = 83) and 6221 controls from nine prospective cohorts in Europe, North America and Australia in the HPV Cancer Cohort Consortium. We described seroprevalence by lead time from blood draw to cancer diagnosis (range: 0-43 years). We found that among oropharyngeal cancers, seroprevalence increased approaching diagnosis for HPV16 E1, E2, E4, E6, E7, L1 and HPV18 E1, E2, L1 (HPV16-E6: from 10.4% at > 20 years to 35.8% at 0-5 years, vs. 0.3% in controls). item.title: Pediatric Recurrent Croup: An International Delphi Consensus Statement.
item.dc:creator: Crotty TJ, Cleere EF, Alhyari F, McBride A, Schaefer S, Heffernan CB
item.description:
Authors: Crotty TJ, Cleere EF, Alhyari F, McBride A, Schaefer S, Heffernan CB
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71022
Published: 2026-Oct-30
PMID: 42963314



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Recurrent croup lacks a consistent diagnostic definition, resulting in substantial variation in investigation and management. We aimed to develop international consensus-based recommendations for the evaluation and management of pediatric recurrent croup. DATA SOURCES: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and EMBASE searched from 1st January 2000 to 15th August 2026, with results reported in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. REVIEW METHODS: An international modified Delphi consensus process was conducted. Panelists rated statements using a 9-point Likert scale across two rounds. Strong consensus was defined as a mean ≥ 8.00 with no outliers; consensus as mean ≥ 7.00 with no more than one outlier. RESULTS: Review of 28 studies confirmed substantial heterogeneity in the definition and investigation of recurrent croup, with most studies at moderate to high risk of bias. Strong consensus was achieved on prioritizing direct laryngoscopy and bronchoscopy in atypical presentations, including subglottic sizing and exclusion of a laryngeal cleft, and limiting allergy testing to children with clinical suspicion of atopic disease. Consensus supported shared otolaryngology-respiratory management, avoidance of routine imaging, and reserving advanced reflux investigation for refractory cases. No consensus was reached on empirical inhaled corticosteroids or antireflux therapy. CONCLUSION: This study provides the first international multidisciplinary consensus guidance for the evaluation and management of recurrent croup, supported by a proposed risk-stratified management algorithm. Agreement on core diagnostic and endoscopic priorities may help standardize clinical practice, while the absence of consensus on optimal medical management identifies clear priorities for future research in a field where high-quality prospective data remain lacking. item.title: DNA Immunotherapy (INO-3107) Long-Term Efficacy Supported by Enhanced Immunogenicity in HPV-6/11 RRP.
item.dc:creator: Amin MR, Belafsky PC, Best SR, Friedman AD, Klein AM, Lott DG, Mau T, Paniello RC, Pransky SM, Saba NF, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Amin MR, Belafsky PC, Best SR, Friedman AD, Klein AM, Lott DG, Mau T, Paniello RC, Pransky SM, Saba NF, et al.
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71016
Published: 2026-Oct-30

Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP), caused by chronic HPV-6/11 infection, leads to repeated papilloma growth requiring frequent surgical removal. DNA immunotherapy INO-3107 aims to induce HPV antigen-specific T-cell responses and reduce surgical burden. This analysis evaluated HPV-specific immune responses after INO-3107 and their association with long-term clinical outcomes. METHODS: Adults with HPV-6/11-associated RRP received INO-3107 in a Phase 1/2 trial and were followed for one year, with additional clinical follow-up in a long-term extension. Number of surgeries in Years 1 and 2 was compared with the pre-treatment year. Blood and laryngotracheal tissue collected at Day 0 and Year 1 were analyzed for treatment-related changes in T-cell activity. Safety was assessed throughout. RESULTS: Thirty-two patients were treated; 28 continued into Year 2. At Year 1, most evaluable patients showed increased T-cell activity: 73% (19/26) demonstrated persistent expanded T-cell populations in blood, 71% (12/17) showed higher T-cell clone counts in laryngotracheal tissue, indicating site-specific immune infiltration. Antiviral T-cell signatures were enriched in 88% for CD4+ Th1 and CD8+ cytotoxic, and 71% for CD8+ effector memory, suggesting durable proinflammatory and memory responses in airway tissue. Mean annual surgeries decreased over time in the overall population (Baseline: 4.1, Year 1: 1.7, Year 2: 0.9). Similar durable reductions were observed in Responder subgroups. INO-3107 was well-tolerated, with no treatment-related serious adverse events. CONCLUSION: INO-3107 generates increased HPV-directed T-cell responses and substantially reduced surgical procedures over two years, supporting its ability to provide long-term clinical benefit in RRP without requiring additional surgeries during the dosing window.

item.title: Efficacy and safety of oral orforglipron in Japanese participants with obesity disease (ATTAIN-J): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 trial.
item.dc:creator: Yokote K, Yamauchi T, Shingaki T, Chin R, Oura T, Nagai Y, Shimomura I, Kadowaki T
item.description:
Authors: Yokote K, Yamauchi T, Shingaki T, Chin R, Oura T, Nagai Y, Shimomura I, Kadowaki T
Journal: The lancet. Diabetes & endocrinology | DOI: 10.1016/S2213-8587(26)00232-9
Published: 2026-Oct-30
PMID: 42962687



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Orforglipron, a small-molecule, non-peptide, oral GLP-1 receptor agonist, has shown bodyweight reduction and cardiometabolic benefits in adults with obesity across phase 3 trials globally. We aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of orforglipron versus placebo for treating obesity disease in Japanese adults. METHODS: ATTAIN-J was a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 trial conducted across 16 medical research centres and hospitals in Japan and included adults aged 18 years or older with a BMI between 27 kg/m2 and less than 35 kg/m2 and two or more obesity-related health disorders, or a BMI of 35 kg/m2 or higher and one or more obesity-related health disorder, with one or more of the obesity-related health disorders being hypertension, dyslipidaemia, or type 2 diabetes (targeted at about 25% of participants), consistent with Japanese indications for tirzepatide and semaglutide for obesity disease; and at least one unsuccessful dietary attempt to lose weight. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) via a computer-generated sequence to once-daily oral orforglipron (6 mg, 12 mg, or 36 mg) or placebo. Co-primary endpoints were mean percentage change in bodyweight and percentage of participants with at least 5% bodyweight reduction from baseline to week 72. Efficacy endpoints were primarily evaluated by the treatment regimen estimand in all randomly assigned participants. Safety was assessed in participants who received at least one dose of study treatment. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05931380 (completed). FINDINGS: Between July 31, 2023, and June 19, 2025, 291 participants were screened, of whom 238 (144 [61%] males and 94 [39%] females; mean age 54·1 years [SD 11·2]) were randomly assigned to receive orforglipron 6 mg (n=61), 12 mg (n=57), or 36 mg (n=60), or placebo (n=60); 214 (90%) participants completed the study. At week 72, mean percentage change in bodyweight was -5·9% (95% CI -7·6 to -4·2) with orforglipron 6 mg, -8·7% (-10·9 to -6·5) with 12 mg, and -7·9% (-10·0 to -5·8) with 36 mg, compared with -0·6% (-2·1 to 0·8) with placebo (all p<0·0001 vs placebo). At week 72, a bodyweight reduction of at least 5% was seen in 15·2% (SE 4·8; nine of 60) of participants in the placebo group compared with 45·6% (6·1; 28 of 61; p=0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 6 mg group, 60·8% (6·4; 35 of 57; p<0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 12 mg group, and 58·8% (6·5; 35 of 60; p<0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 36 mg group. Adverse events with orforglipron were mostly mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal symptoms. Across all orforglipron groups, treatment-emergent adverse events that most frequently led to study treatment discontinuation were nausea (one [2%] of 61 in the 6 mg group, one [2%] of 57 in the 12 mg group, and five [8%] of 60 in the 36 mg group vs none with placebo) and vomiting (none in the 6 mg group, two [4%] in the 12 mg group, and one [2%] in the 36 mg group vs none in the placebo group). INTERPRETATION: In Japanese adults with obesity disease, once-daily orforglipron resulted in statistically superior reductions in bodyweight versus placebo, with a safety profile consistent with that of other GLP-1 receptor agonists. item.title: Efficacy of immediate radiotherapy versus salvage radiotherapy in patients with de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma responsive to chemoimmunotherapy.
item.dc:creator: Zhang QT, He JR, Guo HB, Sun YN, Chen J, Cheng H, Xiao YX, Sun XS, Wu LF, Li XY, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Zhang QT, He JR, Guo HB, Sun YN, Chen J, Cheng H, Xiao YX, Sun XS, Wu LF, Li XY, et al.
Journal: ESMO open | DOI: 10.1016/j.esmoop.2026.108608
Published: 2026-Oct-30
