Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chemoimmunotherapy has become the standard first-line treatment for de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (dmNPC). However, the role and optimal timing of locoregional radiotherapy in dmNPC in the chemoimmunotherapy era remain unclear. This study aims to evaluate whether salvage locoregional radiotherapy (SLRRT), deferred until locoregional progression in patients with well-controlled distant metastases, compromises survival compared with immediate locoregional radiotherapy (ILRRT) in responders to first-line chemoimmunotherapy. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with dmNPC who achieved a complete or partial response after first-line platinum-based chemotherapy combined with anti-programmed cell death protein 1 therapy. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS). Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was applied to adjust for baseline characteristics. Survival outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analyses and a multivariate Cox regression model. RESULTS: A total of 439 patients were included, with a median follow-up of 35.0 months (interquartile range, 24.0-45.2). Of these, 331 patients were assigned to the ILRRT cohort and 108 to the SLRRT cohort. After IPTW adjustment, SLRRT was not associated with inferior OS compared with ILRRT [2-year OS, 97.4% versus 90.1%; hazard ratio (HR) 0.93, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.54-1.59, P = 0.78]. SLRRT was associated with worse locoregional control (HR 4.78, 95% CI 2.98-7.66, P < 0.001) but better distant control (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.41-0.95, P = 0.03). Radiotherapy-related adverse effects were substantially more frequent in the ILRRT cohort. CONCLUSIONS: Deferring SLRRT until locoregional progression did not compromise survival among responders to first-line chemoimmunotherapy. These findings support a response-adapted, de-escalated treatment strategy that may reduce treatment-related toxicities and improve quality of life without adversely affecting survival.

item.title: Mechanism study on CSF3-Induced M2 polarization of tumor-associated macrophages and CCL9 secretion in promoting tumor progression in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Xie Y, Lin Y, He J, Ji Y, Luo X, An W, Sun Y, Qiao X, Li Z
item.description:
Authors: Xie Y, Lin Y, He J, Ji Y, Luo X, An W, Sun Y, Qiao X, Li Z
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108176
Published: 2026-Oct-30
PMID: 42962475



Abstract:
Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) accounts for ∼85% of head and neck cancers and is the sixth most common malignancy worldwide. Standard surgery plus chemoradiotherapy has limited success due to high recurrence. Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) in the tumor microenvironment (TME) promote tumor growth, invasion and angiogenesis. Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor 3 (CSF3) regulates neutrophil function and may influence monocyte differentiation into M2 macrophages in breast and bladder cancers. This study aims to investigate CSF3's role in promoting TAM-M2 polarization in HNSCC and explore the mechanisms using in vitro and in vivo approaches. Bioinformatic methods analyzed CSF3's clinicopathological significance and association with M2 infiltration. CSF3 expression was evaluated in paired tumor/normal tissues by RT-qPCR and IHC, and serum levels by ELISA. CSF3-modulated cell lines were co-cultured with TAMs; polarization was assessed via marker expression by RT-qPCR and flow cytometry. CSF3-overexpressing mouse models examined tumor growth and CD206 expression by IHC. Functional assays on MOC2 cells used TAM-conditioned supernatant. RNA-seq and CCL9 secretion were analyzed. CSF3 correlated with poor prognosis and increased M2 infiltration. Elevated CSF3 mRNA/protein were detected in tumor tissues and serum. CSF3 overexpression promoted M2 polarization, CD206 expression, and tumor growth. Conditioned medium from TAMs co-cultured with CSF3-knockdown tumor cells attenuated MOC2 proliferation, migration and invasion. Tumor-derived CSF3 upregulated TAM-derived CCL9, and exogenous CCL9 restored pro-tumor effects. Elevated CSF3 in HNSCC promotes TAM-M2 polarization and induces CCL9 production in polarized TAMs, creating a pro-tumor microenvironment that facilitates HNSCC progression.

item.title: Age-specific income losses due to HPV-attributable cancers in Singapore.
item.dc:creator: Blythe R, Graves N, Iyer NG, Peres MA
item.description:
Authors: Blythe R, Graves N, Iyer NG, Peres MA
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361921
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42961926



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The link between Human Papillomavirus (HPV) and cancer is well-established. In Singapore, bivalent HPV vaccines are subsidised for females, but not males. Economic analysis of HPV vaccination has generally assessed the costs to the health system, but this may not be as relevant to individual decision-making as potential lost income. We estimated the impact of bivalent HPV 16/18 vaccination on sick leave, unemployment, and premature mortality as a function of age and sex to understand the broader impact of HPV-related cancers. METHODS: We developed a population-level economic model to estimate lifetime income losses by diagnosis age, sex and cancer type. We applied sex- and cancer-specific Cox regressions to the Singapore Cancer Registry for annual predicted survival from 1992 to 2022. These were combined with census and employment data to estimate HPV-associated income losses in Singapore. Attributable fractions and vaccine effectiveness data for HPV 16/18 from the literature were used to estimate the effectiveness of bivalent HPV vaccination. Structural sensitivity analysis examined the role of 80% population coverage conferring herd immunity. RESULTS: The registry contained 17,294 individuals with an HPV-associated cancer diagnosis. Lost income was greatest for cervical cancer due to its high prevalence, however the losses per diagnosis were highest for oropharyngeal cancer. Bivalent HPV vaccination led to income benefits of $SGD1,397 [$895 to $1,838] in girls and -$62 [-$76 to -$48] in boys. CONCLUSIONS: In addition to avoiding healthcare costs and lost quality of life, parents should consider vaccination as a means of avoiding potential income losses. A national policy of gender-neutral HPV vaccination could deliver substantial income protection due to both individual vaccine protection and herd immunity.

item.title: Edentulism and functional disability in older adults: A longitudinal and cross-national study in England, the United States, and India.
item.dc:creator: Tang W, He L, Zhang M, Li J
item.description:
Authors: Tang W, He L, Zhang M, Li J
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361422
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42961862



Abstract:
Edentulism may contribute to functional disability in older adults, yet cross-national evidence combining multiple analytic strategies and mechanistic assessment remains limited. This study examined the association between edentulism and disability in activities of daily living (ADL) and instrumental activities of daily living (IADL) across England, the United States, and India. We analyzed harmonized data from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA; n = 9,102), the Health and Retirement Study (HRS; n = 22,156), and the Longitudinal Ageing Study in India (LASI; n = 31,816) for adults aged 60 years or older. Cross-sectional associations were estimated using inverse probability weighting (IPW) and augmented IPW. Longitudinal Cox proportional hazards models were applied in ELSA and HRS. Mediation through grip strength, body mass index (BMI), and depressive symptoms was assessed with counterfactual causal mediation analysis on the risk-difference scale. Edentulism was associated with higher odds of ADL (pooled odds ratio 1.30, 95% confidence interval 1.20-1.42) and IADL disability (1.27, 1.11-1.45). Longitudinal analyses confirmed elevated hazard ratios for incident ADL (1.19, 1.09-1.30) and IADL disability (1.30, 1.19-1.43). Grip strength accounted for the largest proportion mediated (approximately 50% in ELSA and HRS, and 5-14% in LASI); BMI and depressive symptoms showed little mediation. In LASI, denture use among edentulous participants was associated with lower disability odds. Edentulism was consistently associated with functional disability across three countries, with grip strength partially accounting for this association, although the cross-sectional design precludes establishing temporality. Oral rehabilitation may partly buffer this risk and merits further prospective investigation.

item.title: Academic Attributes and Institutional Characteristics of U.S. Otolaryngology-Head & Neck Surgery Residency Program Directors.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the academic attributes and appointment patterns of current U.S. Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery residency program directors (PDs). STUDY DESIGN: Cross-sectional analysis accredited Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery residency programs in the United States. METHODS: One hundred and twenty six U.S. otolaryngology program directors were analyzed. RESULTS: We found that 63.5% (80/126) of PDs are male, and nearly half (49.2%; 62/126) completed some training at their current institution, while most were later promoted internally after joining the faculty. Advanced degrees (PhD, MBA, MPH) were held by 18.3% (23/126) and were associated with nearly double the publication output (80.0 vs 40.8 publications; P < .01). External hires accounted for 8.3% (10/120) and trended toward higher H-index values (17.4 vs 12.0, P = .25), total publications (94.9 vs 45.4, P = .226), and NIH funding rates (10.0% vs 2.7%, P = .30) than internal hires. A significant portion of PDs hold additional advanced degrees, which are associated with increased academic productivity. For those considering a career in educational leadership, understanding prevailing academic backgrounds and institutional hiring patterns may help inform career planning.

item.title: Immunotherapy for Head and Neck Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma with Perineural Spread: A Systematic Review.

item.description:

Published: 2026-Oct-29

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immunotherapy is increasingly used for head and neck cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) with perineural spread (PNS), though outcomes remain poorly defined. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA and MOOSE guidelines. Studies reporting immunotherapy in cSCC with clinical or radiologic cranial nerve PNS were included. Data on demographics, nerve involvement, treatment, response, and outcomes were extracted. RESULTS: Twenty-three studies (150 patients) were included. Median age was 72.5 years; 78.5% were male. PNS most commonly involved CNV (83.3%) and CNVII (31.7%). Immunotherapy was primarily cemiplimab (75.2%) and pembrolizumab (19.7%). Disease control was achieved in 87.3% (complete response: 38.7%, partial response: 42.0%). Functional nerve recovery was reported in 26/64 patients with evaluable outcomes (40.6%), equivalent to 17.3% of the total cohort. Median follow-up was 16 months, with 82.3% alive. Adverse events occurred in 28%, with serious toxicity rare. CONCLUSIONS: The available evidence demonstrates that immunotherapy can achieve disease control in cSCC with PNS and that established cranial nerve dysfunction may recover in some patients. Prospective studies with standardized oncological and functional outcomes are needed to better define treatment efficacy and establish the role of immunotherapy within current treatment paradigms.

Abstract:
Despite their considerable promise, many current medical foundation models remain modality specific and lack transparent reasoning, limiting clinical adoption. To address this gap, we introduce Explainable Vision Language Foundation Model for Medicine (EVLF-FM), a multimodal vision language foundation model that combines broad diagnostic capabilities with fine-grained explainability. The development and testing of EVLF-FM encompassed more than 1.3 million total samples from 18 global datasets across 10 imaging modalities related to six clinical specialties: dermatology, hepatology, ophthalmology, pathology, pulmonology and radiology. In internal validation for disease diagnostics, EVLF-FM achieved the highest average accuracy, 0.895, outperforming leading generalist and specialist models. In medical visual grounding, EVLF-FM also achieved reasonable performance across nine modalities with average accuracy at 0.5 intersection over union (Acc@0.5) of 0.842. External testing further confirmed consistent zero-shot and few-shot performance, with competitive F1 scores despite a smaller model size. Human evaluation of these reasoning outputs using the S.C.O.R.E. framework yielded a high overall mean score of 4.25/5, supporting their clinical interpretability. Current limitations include the need for additional validation across diverse healthcare settings. Prospective clinical studies are required to evaluate the safety, effectiveness and clinical utility of EVLF-FM before routine clinical deployment.

Abstract:

item.title: Improved model predictive current control strategy for overvoltage suppression in long-cable PWM-driven induction motor electrical submersible pump systems.
item.dc:creator: Gong X, Qi X, Feng M, Zhu L, Wang N
item.description:
Authors: Gong X, Qi X, Feng M, Zhu L, Wang N
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360296
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42956049



Abstract:
Long-cable PWM-driven induction motor electric submersible pump (ESP) systems suffer from significant voltage reflection issues caused by distributed parameter effects, leading to transient overvoltages at the motor terminals that can reach several times the DC bus voltage. This severely threatens system stability and motor insulation integrity, and traditional control methods prove inadequate for effective suppression. To address this challenge, the paper proposes an improved model predictive current control (MPCC) strategy for induction motor ESP systems, which integrates overvoltage suppression and equivalent switching frequency reduction for long-cable PWM-driven applications. The reflection overvoltage mechanism is thoroughly analyzed through mathematical modeling of the motor and long-cable transmission line, and the applicability of predictive current control in such systems is investigated. The core improvement lies in a circular boundary constrained MPCC combined with a dynamic transition voltage vector selection mechanism, which enables dual-mode optimization based on current error boundary conditions: the normal cost function is applied within the circular boundary to jointly optimize voltage tracking, switching frequency, and dv/dt; while the backup cost function is activated outside the boundary to prioritize current error minimization. This effectively optimizes the voltage switching strategy, reducing both switching frequency and dv/dt, thereby preventing overvoltage excitation caused by abrupt voltage vector steps in PWM-driven systems. Simulation models under different cable configurations (1 km with RLC filter and 110 m without RLC filter) and an experimental platform based on a neutral-point-clamped three-level inverter (NPC-TLI) topology are established, with the 110 m no-filter configuration serving as a direct cross-validation baseline. Comparative simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed strategy significantly reduces the duration of motor terminal overvoltage while maintaining excellent system dynamic performance. Moreover, the improved MPCC effectively suppresses overvoltage and reduces equivalent switching frequency without requiring hardware filter redesign, while the RLC filter remains necessary for full insulation safety compliance under more demanding long-cable conditions, substantially mitigating the risk of motor insulation breakdown.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Achieving early glycemic control in adolescents with diabetes is associated with improved short- and long-term health outcomes. item.title: Identification of prognostic biomarkers for nasopharyngeal carcinoma through microRNA‑mRNA network analysis combined with screening of immune‑related genes.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a common head and neck cancer, and radiotherapy is its main treatment. Recurrence and metastasis are the main causes of treatment failure. Although immunotherapy can prolong patient survival, the molecular mechanisms underlying NPC development and progression remain unclear. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) and their target genes are abnormally expressed in many tumors and are closely involved in tumor development. Target genes of DEMs were predicted with TargetScan, miRDB, and miRWalk, and then intersected with DEGs to identify core genes. A miRNA-mRNA regulatory network was constructed in Cytoscape. The core genes were further overlapped with immune-related gene sets, followed by functional enrichment analysis. A prognostic risk model was established using LASSO-Cox regression, and immune cell infiltration was evaluated with CIBERSORT. Model validation, immunohistochemical analysis, and drug-gene interaction analysis were also performed. In vitro, RT-qPCR was conducted in C666-1 and NP69 cell lines to verify the expression of key genes. RESULTS: We identified 213 potential target genes of key miRNAs. Three miRNAs (hsa-miR-30e-5p, hsa-miR-30a-5p, and hsa-miR-20a-5p) were associated with NPC prognosis, and 17 core immune-related genes were enriched in cytokine-mediated signaling, chemokine response, and JAK-STAT pathways. Drug-gene analysis predicted that 5-fluorouracil targeted LGR5 and aldesleukin targeted SOCS1. RT-qPCR demonstrated that SOCS1 was upregulated approximately 3.7-fold in NPC cells (P < 0.01). item.title: Patient Experiences With ctHPVDNA-Guided Surveillance for HPV-Positive Oropharyngeal Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Fleming GE, Roth H, Hanna GJ, Sethi RKV, Minken J, Mukundan D, Schoenfeld JD, Windon MJ, Rettig EM
item.description:

Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Circulating tumor human papillomavirus DNA (ctHPVDNA) is a potential biomarker for surveillance of HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer. Despite its growing clinical use, patient experiences are not well characterized, and understanding patient perspectives of ctHPVDNA-guided surveillance is essential to guiding its appropriate use while mitigating potential harms. OBJECTIVE: To characterize patient experiences with ctHPVDNA-guided surveillance. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: A mixed-methods cross-sectional interview study in adults treated for HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer with 1 or more surveillance ctHPVDNA test 3 or more months before enrollment conducted in June through August 2025 in a single tertiary academic cancer center. Purposive sampling ensured representation of diverse patient experiences. EXPOSURES: One semistructured interview regarding experiences with ctHPVDNA-guided surveillance. Willingness to pay (WTP) out of pocket was assessed using iterative bidding. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Themes and subthemes were derived from coded interview transcripts using a categorical inductive approach. RESULTS: Among 20 participants (median age, 58 years [IQR, 55-70 years]; 16 males [80%]), 8 (40%) had true-negative ctHPVDNA test results, 6 had true-positive results (30%), 4 had false-negative results (20%), and 2 had false-positive results (10%). Five major themes emerged: (1) broad enthusiasm and support for ctHPVDNA testing, with a common assumption that more and earlier disease-related information is beneficial, and appreciation for the reassurance of negative test results (discordance between support for testing in general and personal experiences of test accuracy was observed); (2) distress as inherent to the emotional variability of the cancer journey itself, such that anxiety associated with ctHPVDNA testing was considered attributable to cancer survivorship rather than to the test; (3) trust in the oncology team supersedes trust in test itself, whereby clinicians were trusted to appropriately interpret potentially confusing results (this trust was enhanced by clear communication); (4) test as a valuable add-on to standard care, which should enrich, but not replace, standard surveillance; and (5) sensitivity to financial toxicity, with strong support for accessible and equitable testing. The median per-test WTP was $325 (range, $0-$9000). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This study found that participants expressed strong support for ctHPVDNA-guided surveillance. Trust in clinicians appeared to mitigate distress related to confusing or inaccurate test results. Clinicians using ctHPVDNA testing should be familiar with and clearly communicate its strengths and limitations to optimize clinical benefit.

Abstract:

Abstract:

This study compared the impact of multimedia versus audio-based educational interventions on the knowledge and self-reported behavior of general dentists in Tehran regarding nutrition and oral health. Knowledge (11 items) and behavior (9 items) regarding the impact of nutrition on periodontal health, dental caries, oral cancer, and erosion were assessed using a validated questionnaire. The educational intervention was delivered over a one-month period. Within-group changes were assessed using paired t-tests, between-group differences using repeated-measures ANOVA, and the effect of demographic variables on post-intervention scores using ANCOVA, with baseline values as covariates (α = 0.05). RESULTS: Of the participants, 53.6% were women, and 37.9% worked in private practice. Both groups demonstrated significant improvements in knowledge and behavior scores following the intervention (p < 0.001), with greater gains observed in the multimedia group. Analysis of covariance indicated that baseline knowledge and behavior were not significantly associated with age, gender, dental school, years of professional experience, or practice setting. CONCLUSION: Both multimedia- and audio-based educational interventions effectively improved dentists' knowledge and self-reported behaviors related to nutrition and oral health. Therefore, given dentists' busy work schedules, the use of these educational approaches may enhance their capacity to provide evidence-based counseling in the field of nutrition and oral health.

item.dc:creator: Bañeras T, Jiménez-Alvarado D, Toledo-Padilla H, Camps-Lahora L, Castro JJ, Espino-Ruano A, Guerra-Marrero A, Couce-Montero L, Meyers EKM, Bañeras L

Authors: Bañeras T, Jiménez-Alvarado D, Toledo-Padilla H, Camps-Lahora L, Castro JJ, Espino-Ruano A, Guerra-Marrero A, Couce-Montero L, Meyers EKM, Bañeras L

Published: 2026-01-01

Abstract:
Shark microbiome studies offer acute insights into host health, immunity, and ecological interactions, yet remain poorly studied compared to other marine vertebrates. Shark-associated microbial communities, despite being species-specific, are influenced by environmental conditions and feeding ecology. In this study, we aimed to characterize shifts in the microbiome of the Critically Endangered angelshark (Squatina squatina) during the early stages of development and to assess how environmental factors contribute to the shaping of a specific microbiota. Samples from thirty-nine juvenile angelsharks were collected from Las Teresitas nursery area in the Canary Islands over one year. Skin, oral and cloacal microbiomes were analysed using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. The sizes of individuals ranged between 24 and 42 cm in length. The shark microbiome was clearly distinct from the surrounding environment, indicating a unique composition from early life stages. Dominant bacteria present in the shark microbiomes included Vibrionaceae (up to 96%), Pseudoalteromonas (up to 63%), Rhodobacteraceae (up to 57%) and Alteromonadaceae (up to 20%). Notably, the abundance of Pseudoalteromonadaceae (assessed by qPCR) was positively correlated with shark growth but was independent of the skin mucus. This suggests a protective role of this phylotype in younger individuals and may help in the adaptation to habitat conditions. Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer has been the leading cause of death in Taiwan since 1982, but long-term survival trends remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated 25-year cancer survival trends, including stage-specific outcomes. METHODS: We analyzed Taiwan Cancer Registry data for patients aged 15-99 years diagnosed with cancer between 1996 and 2021. We estimated the cancer survival index for all sites combined and age- and sex-adjusted 5-year relative survival ratios for individual cancers. The Ederer II cohort method was used for diagnoses before 2018, and the survivorship-period-cohort model was used to nowcast survival for diagnoses in 2018-2020. TNM stage-specific survival was evaluated for 17 cancers diagnosed during 2010-2017. RESULTS: The 5-year cancer survival index increased from 46.8% in 1996 to a nowcast estimate of 56.2% in 2020. Survival improved most for small intestine, lung, and nasopharyngeal cancers, with lung adenocarcinoma also shifting toward earlier-stage diagnosis. Survival declined for cervical, renal pelvis, bladder, brain and CNS, and gallbladder cancers. CONCLUSIONS: Nationwide cancer survival improved substantially, but persistent cancer-specific gaps highlight priorities for early detection, treatment, and cancer control. IMPACT: These population-based estimates provide timely evidence for monitoring cancer prognosis, evaluating cancer-control progress, and identifying cancers and stages requiring greater clinical and public health attention.

Published: 2026-Oct-28

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether preoperative intravenous iron infusion is associated with reduced postoperative packed red blood cell (PRBC) transfusion risk and transfusion volume among patients undergoing head and neck free flap reconstruction. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study. SETTING: Tertiary head and neck cancer centre. METHODS: Adult patients undergoing free flap reconstruction for head and neck cancer between January 2022 and May 2025 were included. Starting June 2022, patients with baseline hemoglobin <130 g/L underwent routine preoperative transferrin saturation testing. Patients with transferrin saturation <20% who subsequently received preoperative intravenous iron infusion were compared with those who did not. Primary outcome was receipt of postoperative PRBC transfusion. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess predictors of transfusion. Negative binomial regression was used to model transfusion volume among transfused patients. RESULTS: Among 324 patients, 32 (9.9%) received preoperative intravenous iron and 59 (18.2%) required postoperative PRBC transfusion. Preoperative iron infusion was not independently associated with postoperative transfusion risk (aOR 1.26, 95% CI: 0.51-3.08, P = .62) or with number of PRBC units transfused (aIRR 1.00, 95% CI: 0.41-2.38, P = .997). Higher preoperative hemoglobin was associated with reduced transfusion risk (aOR 0.96 per g/L increase, 95% CI: 0.94-0.98, P < .001), while advanced tumor stage was associated with increased transfusion risk (aOR 2.55, 95% CI: 1.13-5.77, P = .024). These findings were unchanged in sensitivity analysis restricted to patients receiving iron ≥7 days preoperatively. CONCLUSION: Short-term iron repletion alone may be insufficient to mitigate transfusion requirements, highlighting the importance of earlier and/or more comprehensive anemia optimization strategies in this high-risk population.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Oropharyngeal tumors with a propensity for submucosal spread can be difficult to detect and delineate during endoscopy. To facilitate their detection, we developed an Artificial Intelligence (AI) algorithm to segment tumors and other anatomically significant structures within the oropharynx. STUDY DESIGN: Model development and validation study. SETTING: Tertiary academic medical center. METHODS: We collected videos from 106 patients undergoing pharyngolaryngoscopy, extracted 942 images, and annotated each pixel as one of 12 classes, such as tumor, uvula, and healthy mucosa. We trained an AI algorithm and evaluated its performance in multiclass and tumor-based segmentation. RESULTS: The AI algorithm achieved a recall statistic of 0.93 and a Dice score of 0.79 for tumor detection. High Dice scores were observed for pharyngeal mucosa (0.90), epiglottis (0.88), and vocal cords (0.82). CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that AI can semantically segment all the structures visualized during endoscopy, paving the way for computer-assisted systems for tumor identification and computer-assisted navigation during endoscopy or intubation.

item.title: Study on the Efficacy of Vidian Neurectomy in Combined Ocular-Nasal Therapy for Allergic Rhinoconjunctivitis.

item.description:
Authors: Hu C, Liu G, Li C, Guo R, Wu K, Ding Y
Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70483
Published: 2026-Oct-28

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy of vidian neurectomy (VN) in improving nasal and ocular symptoms in patients with drug-refractory allergic rhinoconjunctivitis (ARC). STUDY DESIGN: A prospective randomized controlled study. SETTING: Yiyang Central Hospital. METHODS: A total of 220 patients with drug-refractory ARC were allocated to the VN (n = 110) and fluticasone propionate (FP) (n = 110) groups. Clinical data, serum, and tear samples were collected at baseline and at 1 week, 2 weeks, 1 month, and 3 months after treatment. Serum immunoglobulin E (IgE), IgG, and IgA levels, tear meniscus height (TMH), tear break-up time (TBUT), tear secretion (via Schirmer's test [SIT]), and eosinophil cationic protein (ECP) and histamine (HA) were assessed. A 1-year follow-up was conducted to evaluate complications and recurrence, and the Kaplan-Meier curves were plotted to show the recurrence rates. RESULTS: Following treatment, patients in the VN group showed reduced serum IgE, IgG, IgA, ECP, and HA levels, and Visual Analog Scale (VAS), Sino-Nasal Outcome Test-20, Total Nasal Symptom Score, corneal fluorescein staining, and Rhinoconjunctivitis Quality of Life Questionnaire scores, and increased TMH, TBUT, and SIT. Both groups demonstrated symptom relief (reduced VAS scores); however, the VN group achieved greater and more sustained improvement, particularly at 3 months, whereas the FP group plateaued after 1 month. Although complications were more frequent in the VN group, the 1-year recurrence rate was lower. CONCLUSION: VN significantly improves nasal and ocular symptoms, reduces immunologic and inflammatory markers, and lowers short-term recurrence in drug-refractory ARC, indicating favorable clinical potential.

item.title: Comparative Effectiveness and Safety of Energy Devices for Thyroidectomy: An Outcome-Specific Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

Authors: Kim DH, Jang DW, Hwang SH
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70524
Published: 2026-Oct-27
PMID: 42947529



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We performed an outcome-specific network meta-analysis comparing contemporary energy devices in thyroidectomy. METHODS: Randomized controlled trials comparing conventional hemostasis with Harmonic, LigaSure, Thunderbeat, or other advanced energy devices during thyroidectomy were included. Frequentist random-effects network meta-analyses were performed per outcome, with treatments ranked by P-scores and consistency assessed via design-by-treatment interaction and node-splitting analyses. RESULTS: Compared to conventional hemostasis, Harmonic significantly reduced operative time (SMD, -1.88), blood loss (SMD, -2.29), drainage volume (SMD, -1.77), hospital stay (SMD, -0.74), transient hypocalcemia (OR, 0.61), transient recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy (OR, 0.63), and postoperative bleeding (OR, 0.56). LigaSure improved operative efficiency but showed less consistent recovery and safety benefits. Harmonic ranked highest across most outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: Harmonic showed the most favorable relative effects across the evaluated outcomes. However, these findings do not establish overall device superiority; selection should consider absolute benefits and device-specific characteristics.

item.title: Targeting Engrailed-1 Fibroblasts in Idiopathic Subglottic Stenosis.
item.dc:creator: Saeedi N, Collins SL, Lopez-Fay DC, Li YCC, Abd-Elazem I, Hillel AT, Motz KM
item.description:
Authors: Saeedi N, Collins SL, Lopez-Fay DC, Li YCC, Abd-Elazem I, Hillel AT, Motz KM
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71012
Published: 2026-Oct-27

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Idiopathic subglottic stenosis (iSGS) is characterized by pathologic deposition of extracellular matrix (ECM) secondary to dysregulated fibroblasts. Engrailed-1 expressing fibroblasts have been shown to promote ECM deposition in fibrosis. Verteporfin has been shown to reduce EN1 expression in fibroblasts through YAP/TAZ signaling. However, EN1 expression, YAP/TAZ signaling, and verteporfin treatment have not been investigated in iSGS pathogenesis. METHODS: Biopsies of diseased subglottis and distal healthy trachea of iSGS patients (n = 6) were assessed. qRT-PCR, analysis of iSGS single-cell RNA sequencing data, flow cytometry and immunochemistry were used to compare the expression of EN1. Fibroblasts from diseased iSGS tissue were treated with verteporfin (5 μM) or control and gene and protein expression analysis was performed for EN1, YAP/TAZ pathway and fibrotic genes. RESULTS: The iSGS subglottis demonstrated increased expression of EN1 (fold change = 58.86, SD = 65.12, p: 0.031) compared to controls. Immunohistochemistry analysis of the diseased iSGS subglottis showed that EN1 was densely expressed. Verteporfin treatment of iSGS fibroblasts in vitro led to an 81.75% (SD = 9.28, p: 0.031) reduction in COL1A1 and 22.77% (SD = 17.11, p: 0.031) reduction in COL3A1 gene expression. This was associated with a 26.32% (SD = 28.25, p: 0.031) reduction in EN1 expression and reductions in the YAP/TAZ associated genes AMOTL2, CCN1, CCN2, YAP1, and WWTR1. CONCLUSION: EN1 and the associated YAP/TAZ signaling pathway are increased in iSGS. Verteporfin treatment inhibited YAP/TAZ expression and attenuated EN1 and COL1A1 expression in vitro. Targeting EN1 expressing fibroblasts through inhibition of YAP/TAZ signaling represents a potential therapeutic target to reduce fibrosis in iSGS. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: N/A.

item.title: Preoperative Inflammatory Ratios Poorly Discriminate Malignant From Benign Parotid Tumours.
item.dc:creator: Kim JM, Jeon SY, Lee YC, Kim SI, Eun YG
item.description:
Authors: Kim JM, Jeon SY, Lee YC, Kim SI, Eun YG
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70536
Published: 2026-Oct-27

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether preoperative blood inflammatory ratios discriminate malignant from benign parotid tumours. METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study included 204 patients undergoing parotidectomy (45 malignant, 159 benign); inflammatory-index analyses included 45 malignant and 157 benign cases. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratios were the two primary indices. Group differences were tested non-parametrically with multiplicity control, discrimination by receiver operating characteristic analysis and association by multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: Median neutrophil-to-lymphocyte and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratios were higher in malignant tumours (2.00 vs. 1.81 and 0.203 vs. 0.166), but effect sizes were small. Areas under the curve were 0.608 (95% confidence interval 0.518-0.701) and 0.631 (0.520-0.735), respectively. At the sample-derived neutrophil-to-lymphocyte threshold, sensitivity was 86.7% and specificity 35.7%. Additional inflammatory indices, histological subgroup analyses and sensitivity analyses did not materially improve discrimination. CONCLUSIONS: Although the two primary ratios were higher in malignant tumours, their distributions overlapped substantially and discrimination was poor. These findings do not support their use as stand-alone markers for preoperative malignancy risk stratification.

item.title: Metabolic heterogeneity of obesity.
item.dc:creator: Smith GI, Petersen MC, Hartig SM, Klein S
item.description:
Authors: Smith GI, Petersen MC, Hartig SM, Klein S
Journal: Nature medicine | DOI: 10.1038/s41591-026-04718-7
Published: 2026-Oct-27
PMID: 42946879



Abstract:
Multi-organ-system insulin resistance is the key pathogenic driver of obesity-related metabolic complications and diseases, such as atherogenic dyslipidemia, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and type 2 diabetes. However, there is considerable heterogeneity in insulin sensitivity among people with obesity. Some are considered to have metabolically healthy obesity, with normal insulin sensitivity in conjunction with normal fasting blood glucose, oral glucose tolerance, plasma lipid profile and intrahepatic triglyceride content. In this Review, we discuss metabolic differences at the cellular, organ-system and systemic levels between people with metabolically healthy and metabolically unhealthy obesity; we also discuss heterogeneity in the therapeutic effects of weight reduction. A better understanding of the differences between metabolically divergent groups and the physiological responses to weight loss can help identify the factors responsible for the link between excess adiposity and metabolic dysfunction and disease.

item.title: Multidimensional Analysis of Immune Rejection in a Murine HLA-Mismatched Laryngeal Transplant Model.
item.dc:creator: Song Y, Li X, Wu T, Yu R, Gu D, Wang H, Liu J, Zhao Y, Ren J, Chen F
item.description:
Authors: Song Y, Li X, Wu T, Yu R, Gu D, Wang H, Liu J, Zhao Y, Ren J, Chen F
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.70987
Published: 2026-Oct-27
PMID: 42946397



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To establish a murine heterotopic laryngeal transplantation (LT) model with a single HLA-A2 mismatch and to develop a multidimensional framework for dynamic evaluation of immune rejection and graft injury. METHODS: Laryngeal grafts from HLA-A2 transgenic mice were transplanted into C57BL/6 recipients to generate an HLA-mismatched LT model, with syngeneic C57BL/6 → C57BL/6 transplants as controls. A multidimensional evaluation system was established, integrating physiological monitoring (survival, body weight, graft appearance, neck circumference, computed tomography, and ultrasonography), immunological profiling (histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and flow cytometry), and inflammatory assessments (cytokines and biochemical parameters) from Day 0 to 12 weeks posttransplantation. RESULTS: Compared with syngeneic transplantation, the HLA-mismatched group showed aggravated immune rejection and graft injury. Progressive graft volume reduction was an early discriminator, detectable at 1 week posttransplantation and correlating with graft surface darkening and ulceration. Immunophenotyping revealed early CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell infiltration beginning at 1 week, whereas regulatory T cells increased at 3 days before markedly declining. Cytokine profiling showed elevations of MIP-1β, G-CSF, and IL-10 from 4 weeks onward, consistent with immune activation and graft injury. CONCLUSION: A murine heterotopic LT model with an HLA-A2 mismatch was established, demonstrating that a single HLA Class I disparity was sufficient to drive progressive immune rejection and graft injury in LT. A panel of biomarkers associated with adverse graft outcomes was observed, providing indicators for monitoring HLA-driven immune injury. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: N/A.

Published: 2026-Oct-27

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess whether e-cigarette use is associated with subsequent health symptoms over time among young people in the United States. METHODS: Logistic regression analyses of online survey data from seven waves (2020-2025, N = 5917) of a probability-based longitudinal cohort (aged 15-24 years at enrollment) tested the association between e-cigarette use duration and subsequent persistent symptoms, controlling for other tobacco use, baseline self-rated health, and demographic characteristics. RESULTS: Compared with no use, sustained e-cigarette use was associated with greater odds of persistent respiratory, somatic, and oral health symptoms at later waves. item.title: Pazopanib alternating with bevacizumab in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to treatment: a multicentre, single-arm, phase 1/2 trial.
item.dc:creator: George S, Vaishampayan U, Hutson A, Groman A, Pili R, Green K, Herbst L, Kallicharan-Smith R, DiRaddo AM, Farrell E, et al.
item.description:
Authors: George S, Vaishampayan U, Hutson A, Groman A, Pili R, Green K, Herbst L, Kallicharan-Smith R, DiRaddo AM, Farrell E, et al.
Journal: The Lancet. Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/S1470-2045(26)00394-3
Published: 2026-Oct-27
PMID: 42945979



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) are considered the backbone for the treatment of metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. We hypothesise that the administration of bevacizumab during scheduled breaks in pazopanib (TKI) treatment can improve tolerability and prolong progression-free survival compared with historical controls. METHODS: In this single-arm, phase 1/2 trial in five US academic cancer centres, patients (aged ≥18 years) with histologically confirmed metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 or less, and adequate organ functions were included. The phase 1 portion included patients with up to one previous therapy with high-dose IL-2 or an anti-PD-1 compound alone or in combination with a CTLA-4 inhibitor. The phase 2 portion enrolled only patients with treatment-naive metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. The primary endpoint of phase 1 was to find the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D). We tested a novel regimen using four dose levels: oral pazopanib (600 or 800 mg daily on days 1-28, followed by a 7 day break) alternating with intravenous bevacizumab (5, 7·5, or 10 mg/kg, one on day 36 and one on day 50) on a 10-week cycle in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to TKI treatment. The primary endpoint of phase 2 was median progression-free survival, assessed by a masked central statistician review. Dose selection (in patients who had completed 15 weeks) and activity (in patients who had completed one full 10-week cycle of the novel regimen) were analysed in the per-protocol population. Safety analyses included all patients who received any treatment. This trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01684397) and is ongoing but closed to new participants. FINDINGS: Between Nov 21, 2012, and June 11, 2018, phase 1 enrolled 25 patients, with 18 patients evaluable for dose-limiting toxicity during the extended 15-week safety assessment period. The RP2D was established as pazopanib 800 mg daily (days 1-28) and bevacizumab 10 mg/kg on days 36 and 50 of a 10-week cycle. Between Jan 23, 2019, and Oct 19, 2023, phase 2 enrolled 53 patients, of whom 51 (including six from phase 1) were evaluable for activity and 59 were evaluable for safety. 36 (71%) patients were male and 15 (29%) were female, and 48 (94%) patients were White. 33 (65%) patients in phase 2 had favourable risk per the International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium categories. After a median follow-up of 63·7 months (IQR 16·2-73·5), median progression-free survival was 24·8 months (95% CI 17·2-34·3). The most common grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events were hypertension (20 [34%] of 59) and elevated aspartate aminotransferase (seven [12%]) and alanine aminotransferase (ten [17%]). Five (8%) patients discontinued the study for drug-related serious adverse events. No treatment-related deaths occurred. INTERPRETATION: The phase 1 portion identified the safe RP2D. The phase 2 portion showed that this novel regimen has promising antitumour activity in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma in the predominantly favourable risk group who are naive to treatment. Phase 3 randomised controlled trial data are needed to confirm these findings. FUNDING: The Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center (RPCCC), US National Cancer Institute (NCI), Novartis.

item.title: Chemoradiotherapy versus radiotherapy as adjuvant treatment for head and neck adenoid cystic carcinoma: a meta-analysis.
item.dc:creator: Young TC, Yap WK, Chang KP, Lee YC, Lin CH, Cheng-En Hsieh R, Kang CJ, Fang KH, Tsai YT, Chen PY, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Young TC, Yap WK, Chang KP, Lee YC, Lin CH, Cheng-En Hsieh R, Kang CJ, Fang KH, Tsai YT, Chen PY, et al.
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108193
Published: 2026-Oct-27

Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The benefit of adding chemotherapy to postoperative radiotherapy for head and neck adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) remains uncertain. We compared adjuvant chemoradiotherapy (CRT) with radiotherapy (RT) alone. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception through May 6, 2026, with manual reference-list checking. Comparative studies reporting time-to-event outcomes for CRT versus RT were eligible. Hazard ratios (HRs) were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and the Hartung-Knapp adjustment. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261485857). RESULTS: Eight studies contributed 836 outcome-specific observations. CRT was not associated with improved overall survival (six studies; 648 patients; HR, 0.99; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.70-1.41; I2 = 0%), disease-free/progression-free survival (five studies; 534 patients; HR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.81-1.34; I2 = 0%), or distant metastasis-free survival (six studies; 574 patients; HR, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.55-1.63; I2 = 44.5%). Neither locoregional control (two studies; 354 patients; HR, 0.09; 95% CI, 0.00-59.00) nor locoregional failure-free survival (three studies; 262 patients; HR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.32-2.60) improved significantly; both estimates were imprecise. Results were consistent in adjusted-versus-unadjusted subgroup and leave-one-out analyses. CONCLUSION: Available nonrandomized evidence does not demonstrate that adjuvant CRT improves survival compared with RT alone in head and neck ACC. Evidence for locoregional outcomes remains sparse and imprecise. These findings do not support routine chemotherapy but favor individualized treatment decisions.

item.title: Competence narrowing in AI-assisted oral English instruction: A quasi-experimental study of the spiral synergy framework.
item.dc:creator: Zhang J
item.description:
Authors: Zhang J
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0357515
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42945343



Abstract:
The rapid integration of generative AI tools into spoken English instruction has produced measurable fluency and accuracy gains, but whether these are evenly distributed across the dimensions of communicative competence remains underexplored. This quasi-experimental study compares the Spiral Synergy Framework (SSF), a three-layer pedagogical sequence (AI Consolidation, Bridging Tasks, Interpersonal Activation), against conventional AI-integrated instruction in two intact Business English classes at a Chinese higher vocational college (experimental n = 36, control n = 34), using oral recordings at three time points scored on five competence dimensions, 15 weeks of classroom observation, and an intra-rater reliability check. The two classes differed significantly at baseline on the oral composite score and three of five dimensions (control higher), though not on CET-4 proficiency or questionnaire items. Because treatment is confounded with class membership and both classes received AI-assisted practice, findings are reported as associations rather than demonstrated causal effects. Linear mixed-effects models testing Group × Time interactions across five outcomes (four dimensions and the composite), corrected for multiple comparisons, identified one outcome - real-time responsiveness - on which the classes diverged: the experimental class maintained responsiveness across the semester while the control class declined despite its baseline advantage (Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted p = .029), a result that held under a cluster-robust sensitivity check. No corrected between-group difference was found for improvisation, coherence, naturalness, or the composite score; improvisation declined descriptively in both classes over the semester. Classroom observation data (experimental class only) document a recurring, non-monotonic cycle of AI-dependency reduction and rebound across 15 weeks. Intra-rater test-retest reliability of the oral-competence ratings was moderate to good (ICC = .67-.91), though this reflects a single rater familiar with participants rather than independent inter-rater agreement. Implications for multidimensional assessment, task sequencing, and cautious interpretation of AI-integrated curriculum research are discussed.

Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361184
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42945291



Abstract:
This study evaluated the oral safety of Sanxan to provide a basis for its application in food. The toxicological characteristics of Sanxan were assessed through an acute oral toxicity test, three genetic toxicity tests, a teratogenicity test in pregnant rats, and a 90-day oral toxicity test. The results showed that no obvious toxic symptoms or mortality were observed in the acute toxicity test, and the maximum tolerated dose was greater than 15 g/kg, indicating that Sanxan had no acute oral toxicity in the test animals. The results of three genetic toxicity tests-the Ames test, the micronucleus test, and the sperm abnormality test-were all negative, and the teratogenicity test in pregnant rats showed no maternal toxicity, embryotoxicity, or teratogenicity, indicating that Sanxan had no mutagenic or teratogenic effects under the tested conditions. The 90-day oral toxicity test showed that Sanxan at doses of 1.3, 2.6, and 5.2 g/kg body weight had no obvious adverse effects on body weight gain, total food intake, total food utilization, hematology, serum biochemistry, organ-to-body weight ratios, or pathological examination in the test animals, and the maximum no-observed-adverse-effect level (NOAEL) was 5.2 g/kg body weight. In summary, under the conditions of this study, Sanxan did not exhibit acute toxicity, genetic toxicity, teratogenicity, or subchronic toxicity, indicating that it has good safety under the tested conditions.

item.title: Airway management and anaesthetic interventions for children with cleft lip and/or palate undergoing general anaesthesia: Protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.dc:creator: Sumi SA, Arin KM, Shams SM, Rafique T, Orchi K, Chowdhury A, Rahman MM, Haque MA
item.description:
Authors: Sumi SA, Arin KM, Shams SM, Rafique T, Orchi K, Chowdhury A, Rahman MM, Haque MA
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361327
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42945279



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children with cleft lip and/or palate may present unique challenges during perioperative airway management because of altered upper-airway and craniofacial anatomy. These children frequently undergo surgical procedures requiring general anaesthesia and airway instrumentation. Several airway-management and anaesthetic techniques have been evaluated to facilitate tracheal intubation and reduce perioperative airway complications, but the comparative evidence from randomised controlled trials has not been systematically evaluated. METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis will include randomised controlled trials involving children < 18 years with cleft lip and/or palate undergoing general anaesthesia. Eligible studies will compare alternative techniques or devices for airway management or other anaesthetic strategies between two groups of cleft lip/palate patients. The primary outcome will be difficulty in tracheal intubation. Where definitions vary substantially, outcomes will be analysed separately or synthesised narratively. Secondary outcomes will include difficult mask ventilation, oxygen desaturation, airway obstruction, difficult laryngoscopy, first-attempt intubation success, number of intubation attempts, time to successful intubation or airway establishment, failed intubation and other perioperative airway or respiratory adverse events. Two reviewers will independently select RCTs, extract data and assess risk of bias. Risk of bias will be evaluated using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Random-effects meta-analysis will be performed where clinically appropriate. Risk ratios will be used for dichotomous outcomes and mean differences or standardized mean differences for continuous outcomes. Certainty of evidence for important outcomes will be assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. REGISTRATION AND REVIEW STATUS: The review was prospectively registered in PROSPERO on 10 March 2026 (CRD420261326076). Full-text screening and data extraction are ongoing and not yet complete. Protocol amendments are documented transparently in PROSPERO.

item.title: Photobiomodulation versus stabilization splint, both combined with self-management, for acute temporomandibular myalgia: 48-week outcomes of a partially randomized controlled study.
item.dc:creator: Hoa NN, Do T, Hoang VH, Thanh Dong T, Quyen TTM, Binh TT
item.description:
Authors: Hoa NN, Do T, Hoang VH, Thanh Dong T, Quyen TTM, Binh TT
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360472
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42945268



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Photobiomodulation (LLLT) is used for myogenous temporomandibular disorders (TMD), but longer-term comparative evidence versus stabilization splints alongside structured self-management remains limited. This study aims to compare pain reduction and maximum painless mouth opening after photobiomodulation+self-management (PBM + SM) versus stabilization splint+self-management (OS + SM), with an additional self-management-only comparator (SM), over 48 weeks. METHODS: This partially randomized controlled study enrolled 66 patients with DC/TMD-diagnosed acute masticatory muscle pain. Forty-four participants consenting to intervention were randomized 1:1 to PBM + SM (660-nm diode laser, twice weekly, 10 sessions) or OS + SM (maxillary stabilization splint worn at night, 8 h/day for 2 months). Both intervention groups received the same SM programme (education, habit modification, and jaw exercises for 2 months). A non-randomized convenience group received SM alone (n = 22). Assessments were performed at baseline and weeks 2, 4, 12, 24, and 48. Primary outcomes were VAS pain (0-10) and maximum painless mouth opening (MPMO, mm). Secondary outcomes included masticatory muscle tenderness and Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC). Longitudinal analyses used linear mixed-effects models. RESULTS: All groups improved over time, with earlier improvement in both intervention arms. In the randomized comparison, PBM + SM and OS + SM showed comparable week-48 outcomes for VAS pain and MPMO. No significant between-group difference in masticatory muscle tender points was observed at week 48 after Holm adjustment. Comparisons involving the SM-only group were exploratory. CONCLUSIONS: Over 48 weeks, PBM + SM and OS + SM produced comparable improvements in pain and maximum painless mouth opening, with no significant between-group difference in masticatory muscle tender points at week 48.
